Drone strike on North Darfur court kills at least 35, rights group says Submitted by Victoria Amani Mwaniki Kishoiyian on Mon, 08/03/2026 - 21:29 The attack comes amid heightened Sudanese army drone operations across Darfur Protesters in Warsaw, Poland, hold placards during a protest against the Rapid Support Forces committing mass atrocities in the Darfur region of Sudan, on 8 November 2025 (Neil Milton/Reuters) Off On Sunday, a drone strike, purportedly carried out by the Sudanese army, targeted Sudan's Customary Court in al-Zawiya Ghara, killing at least 35 people and injuring others. All the victims were inside the court building and its immediate surroundings when the attack occurred, according to the Emergency Lawyers Group , which monitors violence against civilians in Sudan. Al-Zawiya Ghara is one of many villages in North Darfur state controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The drone fired at least four missiles at the court building while local leaders conducted a meeting. Among the dead are two RSF field commanders, four tribal elders, and traditional leaders hailing from the Mahameed branch of the Rizeigat, according to the Sudan Tribune. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Sunday's attack comes amid heightened Sudanese army drone operations across Darfur, closing in on RSF positions to weaken the paramilitary group after successive defeats in North Kordofan. The largely RSF-dominated Sudan Founding Coalition, known as Tasis, blamed the Sudanese army for the strike. In the Sudan Tribune, a Tasis spokesperson, Ahmed Tugod Lisan, urged an independent investigation to hold those responsible to account. The Emergency Lawyers Group has demanded an investigation into the drone strike and denounced the targeting of the court, deeming attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure a “grave violation of international humanitarian law”. It further stated that drones are increasingly used to target civilian areas and gatherings, exacerbating the risks faced by the population. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); The RSF also stands accused of committing war crimes, including carrying out drone strikes on civilians over the past three years of the war. The paramilitary group’s siege on el-Fasher, one of Darfur’s largest cities, in October of 2025, bore the “hallmarks of genocide” per a United Nations fact-finding mission. RSF commanders sentenced In early July, the anti-terrorism and crimes against the state court in Port Sudan sentenced RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, and 15 other defendants to death in absentia. UK hosting 'discreet' Sudan event featuring UAE-aligned RSF representatives Read More » According to the Sudan Tribune, they were convicted of their roles in the killing of West Darfur Governor Khamis Abdullah Abakar, crimes against humanity, war crimes, prohibited warfare, and genocide in el-Geneina. Presided over by special judge Mohamed al-Amin, the ruling constitutes the first judicial conviction of the paramilitary group’s leadership since the outbreak of Sudan’s war on 15 April 2023. The trial centred heavily on the 2023 assassination of Governor Abakar, a day after he denounced an RSF shelling on the el-Jamarik neighbourhood. Human Rights Watch concluded in 2024 that actions in the capital of West Darfur, el-Geneina, constituted ethnic cleansing and possibly genocide against the Masalit people and other non-Arab communities. Although video footage circulated online of Abakar’s body being mutilated by known RSF soldiers, the paramilitary group repeatedly blamed the Sudanese Armed Forces and denied responsibility. Middle East Eye reported in June 2023 that around 1,500 people were killed in el-Geneina in the first two months of the war, forcing tens of thousands of Masalit residents to flee el-Geneina and West Darfur on foot to seek refuge across the border in eastern Chad. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Among the trial’s defendants were two brothers of Hemedti: RSF deputy leader Abdel Rahim Hamdan Dagalo and Algoney Hamdan Daglo Musa, also known as al-Qoni. The court also handed down convictions to Abdel Rahman Juma Barkallah, the RSF commander in West Darfur, and al-Tijani al-Tahir Karshoum, the state’s former deputy governor. The court held Hemedti legally responsible for directing the genocide of the Masalit and siege of el-Geneina, citing the systematic destruction and looting of property, as well as deliberate attacks on civilians, residential areas, schools, and places of worship. Dagalo was convicted of co-organising the siege of el-Geneina, the civilian displacement, and the genocide of the Masalit. Qoni was found liable for facilitating the siege, while Barkallah was liable for leading frontline RSF soldiers during systematic assaults on Masalit neighbourhoods. The court ordered the confiscation of all RSF assets and instructed the state to request Interpol red notices to secure the arrest and extradition of those convicted. Israel revels in Spain's migrant crisis while embarrassing ally Morocco Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Sun, 08/02/2026 - 16:19 Israel and the US exploited the deaths of Moroccan migrants to punish Spain for its stance on Gaza and Iran A woman sits by a barbed-wire fence as relatives await the return of people from Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta at the Bab Sebta border crossing near Fnideq, Morocco, 2 August 2026 (Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP) Off Israeli political leaders have mocked and exploited the migration crisis engulfing Morocco , an Israeli ally, and Spain , whose relations with Israel have sharply deteriorated. Israel's ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, wrote on X last week with barely concealed glee: "Spain, which never misses an opportunity to lecture Israel, has declared a state of emergency in Ceuta following the crisis over its immigration policy." Spain did not declare a state of emergency in Ceuta . Danon's real grievance appears to be Madrid's forceful and consistent condemnation of Israel's genocide against Palestinians in Gaza, along with its refusal to back the US and Israel in their war against Iran. "The involvement of official Israeli channels and associated social media accounts in amplifying anti-Spanish rhetoric in the wake of the Ceuta crisis seeks to undermine Spanish strategic positions in the Middle East and North Africa region," Denis Cenusa, a geopolitical analyst and fellow at the Centre for European Policy Analysis, told Middle East Eye. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); "This constitutes clear retaliation for Spain's firm stance on the Palestinian cause and the joint US-Israeli attacks against Iran," he added. More than 60,000 Moroccan migrants attempted to cross from Morocco into Ceuta , a Spanish enclave in North Africa. At least 70 drowned or were crushed in the attempt, a number expected to rise. 'Why did they open the doors' Among the dead was Moroccan footballer Faten Ben Omar El Azizi , who played for Moghreb Atletico Tetuan. "The youth are lost… Who opened the door the first time? Why did they open it so that our children could be killed?" her mother said in a video published by Al Ayoum 24, shortly before Faten was buried in a Tetouan cemetery. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Beyond the grief inflicted on her family, El Azizi's death exposed an uncomfortable truth about the country she represented. Morocco has emerged as something of a footballing powerhouse in recent years: its men's national team ranks sixth in the world, and the state has poured millions of dollars into developing the women's game. El Azizi belonged to the generation that investment was supposed to benefit. Thousands make dramatic sea crossing into Ceuta from Morocco Read More » That investment into the country's human capital looks harder to square with what happened next. According to several reports, the Moroccan state, headed by King Mohammed VI, opened the border gates into Ceuta, known in Morocco as Sabtah, last Thursday. The message to many Moroccans was unmistakable that the route out of the country and into Spanish territory was open. Madrid has so far avoided publicly blaming Rabat, but a source close to Spain's foreign ministry told MEE that officials privately believe the Moroccan state deliberately orchestrated the crisis. Spanish authorities received intelligence about a possible surge in crossings into Ceuta and Melilla ahead of Morocco's Throne Day but failed to act, the Spanish outlet The Objective reported on Saturday. Military and civilian intelligence sources told the outlet that officials repeatedly disregarded warnings, including alerts issued only days before the mass movement began. Observers had already recorded an unusual influx of buses into Fnideq, the Moroccan town closest to Ceuta, before thousands of people converged on the border and crossed into the enclave. 'Spain will pay a price' What Morocco has actually gained from all this remains unclear, beyond politically wounding Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, whose relationship with Washington has also deteriorated. (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({}); Sanchez may well have believed he'd secured lasting peace with Rabat after a diplomatic rupture that ran from December 2020 to March 2022. Fifty years of plunder: How Morocco and its allies profit from Western Sahara Read More » In March 2022 he wrote to Mohammed VI endorsing Morocco's autonomy proposal for Western Sahara, a major shift in Spain's position on the decades-old dispute. A year later he helped bring Morocco into the joint Spanish-Portuguese bid to host the 2030 World Cup, and let the king unveil Morocco's inclusion through his own minister, Chakib Benmoussa. The alliance appears to have been jeopardised by Morocco for reasons no one has yet explained. Before many of the bodies had even been recovered from the sea, Israel's national security minister, Itamar Ben Gvir, offered his "congratulations" to Sanchez "for his profound commitment to welcoming immigration and 'human diversity'." He added: "As someone who demonstrates great concern for Hamas and the residents of Gaza, I call on you to translate words into actions: open the doors of Spain and grant refuge to the residents of Gaza who seek to emigrate." The intervention wasn't aimed at Spain alone. By turning dead Moroccans into ammunition against Madrid, Israeli officials also humiliated a government that normalised ties with Israel on 22 December 2020 and has treated that relationship as a source of diplomatic leverage ever since. Israel and the US have both started questioning Spain's hold over Ceuta and Melilla altogether. Earlier this year, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, wanted for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza, accused Sanchez's government of waging a "diplomatic war" and warned it would not be allowed to continue "without paying an immediate price." Spanish commentators accuse Israel and US of involvement in Ceuta crisis Read More » "Israel will not remain silent in the face of those who attack us," he said. Many analysts now suspect this was that price. "The Israeli ambassador to the UN and unofficial accounts on X have been amplifying anti-colonial rhetoric directed against Spain. Their emergence coincided with the height of the crisis, which could indicate a degree of coordination," geopolitical analyst Cenusa said. In Washington, a House Appropriations Committee report published on 30 April described Ceuta and Melilla as Spanish-controlled cities "located in Moroccan territory" and urged the secretary of state to push negotiations over their status. The wording appeared only in a report attached to the bill, not the bill itself, but it read as a signal to Spain, a Nato member. The House passed the legislation on 15 July; the Senate has not, and the president has not signed it. No hard evidence has emerged that Israel, the US and Morocco coordinated the crisis. However, with Israeli leaders openly gloating on social media, at least one member of Sanchez’s government has entertained the possibility. Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente shared a post stating: "Some in Washington, Tel Aviv, and Rabat... wanted images of our security forces and armed forces machine-gunning children on the beach." Bulls in charge as PSX opens week by gaining 2,100 points. The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) opened the week in the green on Monday, gaining more than 2,100 points to close above the 178,000 mark. The development came as global oil prices tumbled on Monday, after United States President Donald Trump said fresh talks with Iran would begin later in the day. At 11am, the benchmark KSE-100 index had gained 2273.78 points, from the previous close of 176,094.11 points. By 2:18pm, the index’s gains had dropped to 1781.72 points. However, after an intraday low of 177,759.88 points, it staged a recovery after 2pm to close at 178,200.02 points — up by 2,105.91 (1.20 per cent) from the previous close. Topline Securities Ltd. said that the rally reflected “renewed risk appetite as investors welcomed signs of easing regional tensions and softer energy prices”. On the index contribution front, FFC, MEBL, LUCK, PPL, and ENGROH emerged as the top contributors, collectively adding approximately 699 points to the benchmark index, according to the firm. Market activity also strengthened: the total traded volume rose to 785 million shares, while traded value stood at Rs33bn, it added. Mettis Global, a web-based financial portal, said the positive momentum at PSX came as “investors took cues from easing geopolitical tensions after Trump called off a planned strike on Iran, reducing immediate concerns over a wider regional conflict”. Awais Ashraf, director of research at AKD Securities, said investor optimism extended the positive momentum from the previous week, driven by expectations of a swift agreement between the US and Iran. “Sentiment improved after the US president announced that talks with Iran would resume on Monday, without setting a deadline for reaching an agreement following the cessation of hostilities,” he said. Ashraf added that “the return of inflation to single digits in July, with the data due to be released today, would provide an additional catalyst for the market by strengthening expectations of monetary easing and further boosting investor confidence”. The KSE-100 index ended the first month of the current fiscal year lower. According to Topline Securities Ltd, the index closed July down 4,208 points or 2.3 per cent month-on-month as escalating US-Iran tensions pushed global crude oil prices higher, weighing on investor sentiment. Average daily traded volume during the month stood at 845 million shares, while average daily traded value was Rs37.5bn. Additional input from AFP

Death toll from suicide bombing near police station in Swat rises to 17. SWAT: The death toll from Sunday’s suicide bombing near a police station in Swat rose to 17 on Monday, including several policemen. The suicide bombing had taken place near the Kabal Police Station while a protest against lawlessness was under way at the adjoining public square. Police said that the suicide bomber had detonated his explosives after police personnel atte­mpted to stop and search him at the entrance to the police station. According to a list of casualties shared by Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi, seven policemen and 10 civilians have lost their lives in the incident while 18 policemen and nine civilians have been injured. Police have revised down the death toll from an earlier tally of 19, which they shared in a statement earlier in the day. Karimi said in the statement that a large-scale rescue operation had been launched immediately after the attack, in which more than 50 Rescue 1122 personnel participated. “Rescue teams provided first aid at the scene before shifting the injured to various hospitals for further treatment. Authorities are continuing relief efforts as investigations into the suicide attack remain under way,” it said. In a separate statement, Swat police said the funeral prayers of two policemen martyred in the suicide attack were held at Javed Iqbal Shaheed Police Lines on Monday. A smartly turned-out police contingent presented a guard of honour to Constable Mukarram Khan and Constable Hussain Khan, and floral wreaths were laid on their coffins. The ceremony was attended by Malakand Regional Police Officer (RPO) Syed Fida Hassan Shah, Swat District Police Officer (DPO) Muhammad Umar Khan, Superintendent of Police (operations) Ghulam Sadiq Khan, Superintendent of Police (headquarters) Ataullah, and other senior police officers. Security personnel and law enforcers have been coming under attack in KP, which continues to face terrorism. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’ (PICSS) monthly security assessment released on Saturday, Security personnel deaths in terrorism incidents in KP, excluding merged districts, increased from 12 in June to 38 in July and terrorist deaths from 37 to 108, reflecting a rise by 192pc. But civilian deaths fell from 26 to seven, a decline by 73pc. One peace committee member was also killed. Security personnel deaths in merged districts rose from six to 11 and terrorist deaths fell from 72 to 55. Civilian deaths, meanwhile, rose by 86pc, increasing from seven to 13. CM visits Swat Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi reached Swat on Monday to meet with the martyrs’ families. He was accompanied by Special Assistant for Home Affairs Tariq Saeed, Chief Secretary Shahab Ali Shah and the KP inspector general (IG) of police, according to a statement issued by the CM office. In Swat, he visited Sheikh Zayed Al Nahyan Hospital in Saidu Sharif and inquired about the health of those injured in the suicide attack. The chief minister directed the hospital administration to ensure the provision of the best possible medical treatment to all the injured, the statement said. It added that the CM also chaired a high-level meeting at the Jirga Hall in Saidu Sharif. At the meeting, which was also attended by senior officials, the CM was briefed on the overall law and order situation in Malakand Division and its Swat district. Reaffirming the government’s commitment to restoring peace, the chief minister said there would be no compromise on law and order in Swat and Malakand. He directed the relevant authorities to launch a full-scale operation against terrorists and ensure that peace and stability were restored. Meanwhile, KP Inspector General of Police (IG) Zulfikar Hameed visited the injured personnel and civilians in the hospital, according to a post on the KP Police’s X account. “Our police personnel have high morale. The cowardly attacks of terrorists will be given a befitting response,” he is quoted as saying. Lawyers, traders observe strike Lawyers across Swat and Upper Swat observed a complete strike on Monday to condemn Sunday’s suicide bombing. Court proceedings remained suspended as members of the legal fraternity expressed solidarity with the victims and called for stronger measures for eliminating terrorism. A shutter-down strike was also observed across Kabal tehsil , where markets remained closed. Separately, elders of the Swat Qaumi Jirga, traders, lawyers, and youth representatives have announced a protest demonstration at Nishat Chowk in Swat’s Mingora on August 7 to condemn the recent wave of terrorism in the region. The organisers said the planned demonstration was aimed at expressing solidarity with the victims of terrorist attacks. It was being organised to demand lasting peace and urge the government to take decisive action against terrorist groups operating in the area, they said.

Islamabad ATC hands Mushtaq Ahmad to police on 3-day physical remand in protest case. ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) has handed over former senator Mushtaq Ahmad Khan and other suspects to police on a three-day physical remand in a case registered in connection with a protest. The police produced the former senator and another person named Daniyal before Duty Judge Rukhsanda Shaheen in the ATC. During the hearing, the prosecution requested a 30-day physical remand of the suspects, stating that the police needed to recover a vehicle and weapons allegedly connected with the case. After hearing the arguments, the court granted the police three-day physical remand of Mushtaq and the other suspects and directed that they be produced before the court again upon completion of the remand period. The first information report (FIR) was registered at Islamabad’s Shalimar Police Station on July 31, on the complaint of Sub-inspector Ghulam Murtaza. The FIR said Mushtaq and dozens of others had led a crowd of about 400-500 people and gathered in the capital’s F-10. It accused the former senator of making “incendiary” speeches on loudspeakers, forcing shops to shut down, and chanting slogans against “current government institutions”. According to the FIR, Mushtaq then led the protesters to Sambal Road with the intention of marching to the Main Jinnah Avenue Road and blocking roads. The FIR said the district administration told Mushtaq through a loudspeaker to end the gathering as it was being held without a no-objection certificate (NOC), but the former senator and others blocked a main road near Shalimar Plaza at around 7:10pm. It accused the protesters of vandalising a media DSNG vehicle and other private cars passing by, along with pelting stones and “attacking” police officials. It further claimed that some protesters snatched away anti-riot helmets from personnel and threatened them. Last Wednesday, Mushtaq’s Pakistan Rights Movement (PRM) alleged that he had been detained by Punjab police on July 28 from Kahuta Bazaar while he was returning from Azad Pattan Bridge after allegedly being denied entry into AJK. Senior police officers in Punjab had not responded to calls and messages at the time. Police officials in Rawalpindi approached by Dawn for comment spoke off the record and denied that Mushtaq was in their custody. Mushtaq’s X account said the next day that he had been released. Following this, he had announced a gathering on July 31 in Islamabad’s F-10 to “express condolences, solidarity with Kashmir and for peace and reconciliation”. Last week, activists in Lahore were detained while holding a peaceful demonstration outside the press club to show solidarity with the proscribed JAAC. Additional input by Mohammad Asghar

PM Shehbaz directs completion of privatisation programmes according to agreed timelines. ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday directed officials to complete all stages of the government’s privatisation programme within the prescribed timelines. Presiding over a meeting in Islamabad reviewing the privatisation of state-owned enterprises, the prime minister instructed relevant ministries and institutions to work in close coordination to ensure that all targets and deadlines under the privatisation programme were met, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). The meeting was attended by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Muhammad Ishaq Dar, Federal Ministers Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Jam Kamal Khan, Ahad Khan Cheema, Sardar Awais Khan Leghari and other senior officials, the PMO said. PM Shehbaz said the privatisation structure for the Zarai Taraqiati Bank Limited (ZBTL) should be designed in a way that safeguards the bank’s primary role in agricultural financing. “It must be ensured that even after privatisation, the Zarai Taraqiati Bank’s focus on providing agricultural loans and financial resources to small and medium-scale farmers remains intact,” he was quoted as saying by the statement. The premier noted that improving farmers’ access to financial resources was “essential” for increasing per-acre agricultural productivity, especially for small and medium-scale cultivators, adding that agricultural development remained critical to Pakistan’s economic growth and food security. Officials from the privatisation ministry briefed the meeting on progress under the government’s privatisation programme and future targets. The meeting was told that 27 state-owned enterprises were included in the programme, which was being implemented in three phases. According to the briefing, the financial closing process for the privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) and First Women Bank has been completed. Officials said the first financial closing and transfer of management control of PIA were completed on June 29. The meeting also reviewed progress on the planned privatisation of Islamabad Electric Supply Company (Iesco), Faisalabad Electric Supply Company (Fesco) and Gujranwala Electric Power Company (Gepco). Officials said expressions of interest (EOIs) had been advertised for these companies, with submission deadlines set for Aug 7 for Fesco, Aug 21 for Gepco and Sep 7 for Iesco. The meeting was also told that international companies have expressed interest in these distribution companies, while roadshows with investors are also underway, according to the PMO. Fesco, Gepco and Iesco collectively serve more than 14 million consumers across major industrial, commercial and urban centres of Punjab, the Islamabad region, and parts of Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The transaction offers investors an opportunity to acquire between 51 per cent and 100pc shareholding, along with management control, in each of the three distribution companies. Officials also updated the prime minister on progress on the privatisation of ZTBL, stating that the transaction structure was being designed to protect the bank’s agricultural lending mandate. The meeting further reviewed progress on the planned privatisation of Islamabad International Airport, Jinnah International Airport in Karachi and Allama Iqbal International Airport in Lahore. The PM directed officials to maintain close oversight of all ongoing privatisation transactions and ensure their completion according to the agreed timelines. The premier issued these instructions three days after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s statement saying that the system had “collapsed”, and that things would not get fixed as long as “the present system is not reset”. Presiding over a separate meeting on private investment, PM Shehbaz directed officials to prepare, at the earliest, a roadmap for establishing a private equity fund to promote investment, support small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and encourage sustainable economic growth, according to his office. He asked officials to submit a comprehensive plan for developing both Pakistan’s public equity market and a private equity fund to improve access to investment capital and help attract foreign investment. “The promotion of private investment is essential for the country’s economic growth,” the premier said according to another statement issued by the PMO. He said that private equity funds could serve as an effective catalyst for investment, business expansion and job creation, adding that sectors including mining, agriculture, livestock, energy and information technology had the potential to become key drivers of Pakistan’s economic growth. PM Shehbaz said a stronger public equity market could provide an important financing avenue for investment in these sectors. He noted that the banking sector’s contribution to investment financing remained limited, making the development of alternative sources of capital increasingly important. The premier noted that the government was prioritising policies aimed at strengthening the economy on a sustainable basis through private sector-led investment, industrial growth and export promotion. DPM Dar, Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani, Special Assistant to the Prime Minister Haroon Akhtar, and senior government officials attended the meeting, the PMO said.

Myanmar's detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi meets Red Cross official. Myanmar’s detained former leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with a representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross on Monday, after years of questions over the health and well-being of the 81-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner. Suu Kyi has been in detention since February 2021, when an elected civilian government led by her was ousted by Myanmar’s military in a dawn coup, plunging the impoverished Southeast Asian nation into turmoil. Since then, Suu Kyi’s exact whereabouts and health condition have been difficult to determine, with no foreign leader or envoy having publicly met with her despite requests for contact from countries in the region that have excluded Myanmar’s leadership from their summits. Suu Kyi met with Arnaud de Baecque, Resident Representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross to Myanmar, in the capital Naypyitaw on Monday, government spokesperson Khine Khine Soe said in a message via Telegram. The ICRC confirmed that a delegate had met with Suu Kyi, without naming the official, while her son described the visit as the first positive development concerning his mother in more than five years. In one of four photographs provided by the Myanmar government spokesperson, Suu Kyi is seen dressed in traditional Burmese attire and standing unaided, shaking hands with de Baecque. In another, they are seated in a sparsely furnished, wood-panelled room containing only two chairs and a desk. This handout photo taken and released on August 3, 2026 by Myanmar’s Presidential Press and Information Bureau (PPIB) shows detained former civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi (L) meeting with Arnaude de Baecque, resident representative of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to Myanmar, in Naypyidaw. — via AFP Son urges continued pressure for Suu Kyi’s release The ICRC said the visit had met with its standards and procedures for visiting people deprived of liberty. “This included the opportunity to speak with Daw Aung San Suu Kyi in private,” it said in a statement, using a Burmese honorific. Suu Kyi’s son, Kim Aris, told Reuters that the ICRC was not able to have a physician examine his mother but he said she seemed to be in good health and in good spirits. “It’s the first independent proof that I’ve had that she’s actually alive for a long time now,” he said in London. “So it’s extremely meaningful.” Aris said that while he remained cautious, he hoped to be able to speak to his mother in time, and urged other governments to keep up the pressure on Myanmar to release her and other political prisoners. Aris told Reuters in December that he had received only sporadic, second-hand details about his mother’s heart, bone and gum problems — and had not heard from her in years. The United Nations, whose special envoy on Myanmar, Julie Bishop, has called repeatedly for independent, verifiable reports on Suu Kyi’s circumstances, said it had taken note of the ICRC announcement and stressed the need for inclusive dialogue. “We welcome this development and reiterate our call for the swift and unconditional release of all those arbitrarily detained, as a fundamental step towards conditions conducive to a credible and transparent political process,” UN spokesperson Farhan Haq told a daily briefing in New York. Detained since coup After a marathon run of secret trials following the 2021 coup, Suu Kyi, who was held under house arrest for a total of 15 years under a previous junta, was sentenced to 33 years’ detention, convicted of charges ranging from corruption and inciting election fraud to violating state secrecy rules. Her allies maintain that the charges were politically motivated and aimed at sidelining the most popular politician in the country of 51 million people. The sentence was later reduced, leaving her with 18 years still to serve, according to a member of her legal team. Myanmar’s military-backed administrations have repeatedly claimed that Suu Kyi, who is the daughter of Myanmar’s independence hero General Aung San, is in “good health”, even as international pressure has grown to allow independent verification. After a meeting between Myanmar’s foreign minister and counterparts from the regional Asean bloc last month, Thailand’s top diplomat Sihasak Phuangketkeow called for access to Suu Kyi. Asean has barred Myanmar’s leadership from its top meetings for failure to implement a peace roadmap. Birthday cake In late April , following a military-engineered election that allowed former junta leader Min Aung Hlaing to become Myanmar’s president, Suu Kyi was moved to house arrest. In another of the photos provided by the Myanmar government offering a rare glimpse inside what appears to be her residence, Suu Kyi is seen cutting a birthday cake, with a clothes rack and storage boxes visible in the background. This undated handout photo released on August 3, 2026 by Myanmar’s Presidential Press and Information Bureau (PPIB) shows detained former civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi cutting a cake in Naypyidaw. — via AFP A fourth photograph is a close-up of the cake, inscribed with “Happy Birthday Aunty Suu 19.6.2026”. Reuters was not able to independently verify the location and the date when the pictures were taken. No earlier version of the pictures was found posted online before Monday.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs331.95 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs389.93 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs110 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs96 per litre on diesel. The Petroleum Division’s notification said the new prices would be applicable for August 4 (Tuesday). The diesel price has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

AJK information secretary says 7 law enforcement personnel martyred in recent unrest. Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Information Secretary Muhammad Rashid Hanif on Monday said that seven law enforcement personnel, including those of police and Rangers, were martyred during recent unrest in the region. The now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now. Clashes took place between protesters and law enforcement personnel in Rawalakot and Mirpur last week, which reportedly resulted in several casualties. Amid the tensions, elections are being held across the region in three phases , with those in Mirpur (July 27) and Muzaffarabad divisions (Aug 2) marred by rigging allegations by the PPP. In a televised address on Monday, Hanif recalled a press conference held on July 27 where a police official presented weapons allegedly recovered from JAAC members. Hanif said that seven personnel were martyred from the “same weapons”, while 45 personnel suffered serious injuries and “numerous” others sustained minor injuries. He further said that police and Rangers vehicles were also burned. “This confirms that the blacklisted JAAC is sheltering a large number of armed elements and is attempting to undermine peace and the writ of the state,” the information secretary asserted. Addressing allegations by JAAC regarding incidents in Rawalakot and surrounding areas between July 27 and July 31, he said they were not only false but “part of a misinformation and propaganda campaign”, which in itself was part of a broader effort to “undermine public order and the writ of the state”. He went on to stress that “security institutions of the AJK government have demonstrated the utmost restraint and professionalism while maintaining law and order”. The information secretary rejected allegations of unprovoked firing by security forces and withholding bodies, stating that the government had no bodies presently in its custody. “Propaganda being circulated by this banned organisation on social media is misleading and part of an effort to further aggravate the situation,” he added, alleging that JAAC members were involved in blocking or burning vehicles carrying essential supplies and food. Hanif also provided the casualty figures for law enforcement personnel resulting from JAAC’s “violent actions” in recent years, noting one police official was martyred in 2024 and three personnel in October 2025 . “Two armed operatives from this organisation recently admitted in their confession that they were promised Rs10 million to kill one Rangers personnel, which raises serious concerns about the source of this group’s funding,” the AJK official claimed. AJK govt calls BBC report ‘biased’; Al Jazeera’s coverage termed ‘selective’ Hanif also termed a BBC report on the Rawalakot clashes as “angled, biased and contrary to the facts”, saying that the AJK government “rejected” it. “The facts and figures presented in this report are not only incorrect, but they were published without verification or confirmation from the government, police or the civil administration,” he stated, describing the report as “contrary to the ethics of journalism and professionalism”. Contending that videos and press releases from the AJK administration had provided evidence of JAAC possessing modern weapons, he noted that the BBC “should have at least taken the verified evidence into account and published a report based on facts”. Similarly, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting criticised Al Jazeera’s coverage of the AJK elections, accusing the Qatar-based broadcaster of “selective reporting from handpicked polling stations” in Muzaffarabad. In a post on X on Sunday night, the ministry alleged that the media outlet had “sought to misrepresent the AJK elections and the voting process” through “carefully chosen timings and scripted statements from selected individuals”. “Such yellow journalism only confirms the agenda of external actors with vested interests who are attempting to delegitimise this electoral exercise and undermine the popular will of the people of Muzaffarabad and AJK,” it alleged. The publication had reported that the residents of Muzaffarabad were observing a boycott of the polls following unrest in the region, where the proscribed JAAC has been protesting for several weeks. Over the past two months, the regional administration and the JAAC have been at odds over various issues, most notably the committee’s demand to abolish the 12 seats in the region’s Legislative Assembly, which has resulted in protests across the region. The government has accused militant elements “pu­r­­s­u­ing a foreign age­nda and backed by Indian funding” of fomenting the recent unrest in AJK. On June 5, following the announcement of the JAAC’s June 9 strike, the AJK government declared the committee a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA). The next day, AJK authorities launched a crackdown on the JAAC, arresting scores of its leaders and later placing 147 of its activists on the Fourth Schedule of the ATA. Last Wednesday, AJK police said that 26 personnel were martyred this year during incidents of unrest as they accused the proscribed JAAC of deliberately targeting law enforcement agencies.

At least 3 killed in rain-related incidents across Punjab; parts of Lahore inundated. LAHORE: At least three people were killed and three others injured in rain-related incidents across Punjab on Monday, while torrential monsoon rains inundated roads and low-lying neighbourhoods in several cities, disrupting traffic, restricting public movement and causing urban flooding. The Flood Forecasting Division (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) on Saturday forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall across parts of Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan until Aug 4. According to a loss and damage report by the Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA), a man was killed and another injured when a house collapsed in Uch Sharif area of Bahawalpur district, while two children drowned in Khushab. Two more people were injured in separate roof collapse incidents in Mandi Bahauddin and Lodhran. The report also recorded a house damaged in Bahawalpur. Separately, authorities reported nine deaths in incidents not directly linked to rain or flooding. These included the drowning of a child in Kot Addu, a man in Narowal, and one man and two children in Attock. Four children also died of suffocation after being trapped inside a car in Mianwali. A PDMA official clarified that these nine deaths did not have anything to do with rain or floods, adding that the victims drowned while trying to bathe and swim in canals and rivers. PDMA Director General Saif Anwar Jappa directed deputy commissioners across Punjab to remain on high alert as the ongoing monsoon spell was expected to continue until Aug 5. He said Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz was personally monitoring the situation and instructed all district administrations, Rescue 1122, Water and Sanitation Agency (Wasa) and other relevant departments to keep their personnel and machinery on standby to respond to any emergency. Jappa said the Provincial Control Room and all District Emergency Operation Centres had been activated and were monitoring the situation round the clock. He directed authorities to ensure the immediate drainage of rainwater from low-lying areas and identified waterlogging points to minimise disruption to public life. He also advised citizens to avoid electricity poles, hanging power lines, dilapidated buildings and mud houses during the rains, urging parents to keep children away from accumulated rainwater. Heavy rain lashed Lahore for several hours, causing extensive waterlogging in many parts of the provincial capital. Rainwater accumulated at levels ranging from one to one-and-a-half feet deep in Township, Kacha Jail Road, Haider Road and Quaid-i-Azam Industrial Estate, submerging several major roads and severely disrupting traffic. Long queues of vehicles formed on inundated roads as commuters struggled to reach their destinations, while residents in affected localities were forced to use alternative routes. Waterlogging in low-lying areas also affected the drainage system, slowing traffic at numerous locations and limiting people’s movement. Residents urged Wasa and the district administration to expedite drainage operations and restore the smooth flow of traffic. According to Wasa Lahore’s monsoon control room, the city received an average rainfall of 24.8 millimetres. The highest level of rainfall was recorded at Wasa Head Office Gulberg (66.4mm), followed by Shadipura (58.8mm), Mughalpura (55.6mm), Mannawan (46.4mm) and Johar Town (45.6mm). Other areas receiving significant rainfall included Tajpura (38.4mm), Farrukhabad (21.8mm), Kahna (20mm), Nishtar Town (19.8mm) and Airport (15mm). Urban flooding was also reported from several other cities, with Faisalabad receiving the heaviest downpour, recording 103mm of rainfall according to the ponding report issued by the Wasa Head Office. Water accumulated up to 23 inches at Chaudhry Flour Mills Chowk, 20 inches at Lower Canal on Jaranwala Road, 19 inches at Saad Bela (People’s Colony No 1), 17 inches each at Riaz Shahid Chowk and Iqbal Stadium, and 15 inches at several locations, including Lasani Pulli, Millat Chowk, 66-Feet Bazar Nishatabad and D Ground. Wasa teams continued de-watering operations at dozens of inundated points across the city. In Gujrat, the maximum rainfall reached 68.8mm, with water accumulating between two and five inches at major locations, including Railway Road, Ghareeb Pura Road, Bhimber Road and Jalalpur Jattan Road. Wasa officials said clearance work was continuing at most locations, although several roads remained partially inundated. Mandi Bahauddin recorded 56.8mm of rainfall at the Wasa Laboratory gauge and 30mm at the Wasa Head Office. Water accumulated up to eight inches on Jail Road, four inches at College Chowk and Committee Chowk, and two inches at several other locations after the rain. In Jhelum, Wasa reported only 0.87mm of average rainfall and said no significant waterlogging remained by the afternoon, with all identified ponding points cleared. The widespread waterlogging was attributed to the intensity of the monsoon downpour, inadequate drainage capacity at several locations and the accumulation of runoff in low-lying urban areas, resulting in traffic congestion, restricted public movement and temporary inundation of residential neighbourhoods. Wasa teams and district administrations continued drainage operations across affected cities throughout the day.

Religious scholar killed in explosion at supermarket in South Waziristan's Wana. LOWER SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: A religious scholar was killed in an explosion, suspected to have been caused by a pressure bomb, at a supermarket in Lower South Waziristan’s Wana on Monday, police said. Wana Circle Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Asghar Ali Shah told Dawn that the explosion occurred on the ground floor of a supermarket located in Rustam Bazaar. He said Mufti Jana Mir Masti Khel sustained critical injuries in the explosion and was immediately shifted to Wana district headquarters hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. The DSP added that he and Wana City Police Station House Officer Usman Wazir, along with a large contingent of police, reached the site of the incident after the explosion, and the area was cordoned off while investigators collected forensic evidence. The DSP said preliminary findings suggested that the pressure bomb had been planted in advance with the apparent intention of targeting the religious scholar. He said police had filed an initial complaint and further investigation was under way to identify the perpetrators and determine the motive behind the attack. In addition to his religious services, Mufti Jana Mir played a significant role in various national peace jirgas held after the 2004 military operations in Wana’s different areas. Most recently, he participated in the Waziristan Peace Jirga, where he presented key recommendations aimed at restoring law and order and achieving sustainable peace in the area. He was widely regarded as a respected religious and social figure who consistently advocated for regional and national interests and worked to promote lasting peace in the region. Monday’s incident comes just three days after unidentified gunmen shot dead Maulana Ismail, a cleric affiliated with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), in Azam Warsak Bazaar of Lower South Waziristan’s Birmal tehsil. On July 28, a local cleric was killed and two other people were injured in a suspected quadcopter attack near a mosque in the Landi Doag area of Birmal. In January, JUI-F leader Maulana Sultan Muhammad Wazir was critically injured in a bomb blast near a madressah in South Waziristan’s Wana Bazaar area and later succumbed to his injuries.

PM Shehbaz congratulates PML-N after party maintains lead in second phase of AJK polls. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the PML-N’s leadership and successful candidates on Monday after unofficial results of the second phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) showed it had won 14 of 19 seats up for grabs the previous day. The PML-N’s main rival in the contest and also its ally in the Centre, the PPP, has accused the PML-N of electoral malpractices, rigging and violence during Sunday polls — as it had during the first phase of the elections in Mirpur division on July 27. The PML-N secured nine of the 13 seats in the first phase while the PPP won the remaining four. Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with polling having been held on seven seats of Muzaffarabad division and 12 refugee seats — reserved seats for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir — on Sunday. In the third phase, elections will be held in 11 constituencies of Poonch division on August 10. ‘Results reflect people’s confidence in PML-N’s policies’ A statement released by the PM’s Office on Monday said the premier congratulated PML-N’s leadership and successful candidates after their win in the second phase. “The continuity of this success is a result of the hard work of PML-N President Nawaz Sharif and the entire PML-N team,” the statement quoted PM Shehbaz as saying According to the statement, the premier noted that Nawaz and the PML-N team had conducted a successful electoral campaign in AJK and the party’s success “reflects the confidence of the people of AJK in PML-N’s policies”. He said the development and prosperity of AJK and the welfare of its people remained PML-N’s top priority. PM Shehbaz added that political parties had actively participated in the second phase of the AJK elections, which he said would further strengthen the democratic process. Results breakdown Earlier in the day, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported the unofficial results of Sunday’s elections, citing AJK Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal’s press talk in Muzaffarabad. During the press briefing, he announced that the PML-N had won 14 seats and the PPP four, the report said. Results LA-25 (Neelum-I) — PML-N’s Ghulam Qadir LA-26 (Neelum-II) — PPP’s Mian Abdul Waheed Khan LA-29 (Muzaffarabad-III) — PPP’s Sardar Mukhtiar Ahmad LA-30 (Muzaffarabad-IV)— PML-N’s Mustafa Bashir Abbasi LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V) — PML-N’s Saqib Majeed Khan LA-32 (Muzaffarabad-VI) — PML-N’s Raja Farooq Haider Khan LA-33 (Muzaffarabad-VII) — PPP’s Dewan Ali Chughtai (as per party claim) LA-34 (Jammu-I) — PML-N’s Nasir Hussain Dar LA-35 (Jammu-II) —PML-N’s Chaudhry Muhammad Ismael LA-36 (Jammu-III) — PML-N’s Muhammad Ahsan Raza LA-37 (Jammu-IV) — PML-N’s Maryam Javed LA-38 (Jammu-V) — PML-N’s Zeeshan Ali LA-39 (Jammu-VI) — PML-N’s Raja Muhammad Siddique Khan LA-40 (Kashmir Valley-I) — PPP’s Amir Abdul Ghaffar Khan LA-41 (Kashmir Valley-II) — PML-N’s Muhammad Amir Shah LA-42 (Kashmir Valley-III) — PML-N’s Syed Shoukat Ali Shah LA-43 (Kashmir Valley-IV) — PML-N’s Muhammad Yasin Lone LA-44 (Kashmir Valley-V) — PML-N’s Ahmad Raza Qadri LA-45 (Kashmir Valley-VI) — PPP’s Abdul Majid Khan Polling was postponed until Tuesday in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kutla) and at 71 of the 174 polling stations in LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat) as polling staff and election material could not reach the constituency because of landslides and bad weather that resulted in blocked roads. According to preliminary results issued by the AJK Election Commission, the refugee seat of LA-37 saw a tough contest between PML-N’s Maryam Javed and Jammu & Kashmir United Movement’s (JKUM) Usman Aleem. Javed emerged as the winner with 28,547 votes, while Aleem was the runner-up with 22,937 votes. According to a document showing results for the refugee seats (constituencies LA-34-LA-45), PPP candidates were the runner-ups to PML-N in LA-36, LA-39, LA-42 and LA-43. All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference was the runner-up in LA-44 and LA-45, while independents placed second in LA-34, LA-35 and LA-41. PML-N now has ‘simple majority’ to form govt: Rana Sana As the unofficial results were released, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs and PML-N leader Rana Sanaullah said his party had now gained the “simple majority” needed to form a government in AJK. He was addressing a press conference alongside Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam. “We have the government-forming number,” he said, adding that “there are a total of 45 seats […] and out of 45, PML-N has so far secured 23 seats”. The PML-N leader said his party had won in four of the seven territorial constituencies in Muzaffarabad while the PPP, which had been “attempting to build a rigging narrative since 10:30am yesterday”, had secured three. Sanaullah demanded that the PPP must tell the people how they managed to secure three seats despite the alleged rigging. “Did they succeed because of rigging or because of a free and fair election?” Sanaullah further stated that the PML-N had also secured 10 out of 12 refugee seats while the PPP had won two. “A democratic government, which has the people’s mandate, will now be formed in AJK, and it will work on ideological, economic, and political affairs of the region,” he said. He added that a parliamentary party session of the PML-N would be called after the conclusion of the third phase of the elections for future decisions. Speaking about PPP’s rigging allegations, the PML-N leader dismissed them and accused PPP of colluding with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) to disrupt the election process in Muzaffarabad. “Anticipating PML-N’s win, PPP along with the action committee planned riots and [..] fired at the police personnel when they got there,” Sanaullah alleged. He claimed that the incident created an atmosphere of fear in the area, which led to a lower turnout. “We received at least 3,000 to 4,000 fewer votes due to this,” he claimed. On PPP’s allegations that an attempt had been made on its candidate AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar’s life, he accused the party of staging a “drama”. He also claimed that the PPP had refused to get Akbar’s medicolegal examination done. Sanaullah accused the PPP of employing “dirty tricks” to sabotage the electoral process, saying that the PPP’s actions violated the Charter of Democracy, in which the party leadership had agreed that they would not “malign each other’s mandate with such dirty tricks”. Replying to a question, he said the PPP had raised doubts over “high turnout” in constituencies where the PML-N’s candidate had won. “With the kind of societal system in place in AJK, it is certainly possible that if there are 300 people in a village, 290 might show up to vote,” he said. He asked the PPP to follow due process in case of complaints rather than “building a narrative and disrupting democracy and the election process”. Federal govt’s last days have begun: Sharjeel On the other hand, PPP’s Sharjeel Inam Memon said his party would continue to contest until the last phase of the AJK elections for the rights of Kashmiris despite what he described as “historical rigging”. Addressing a press conference in Islamabad alongside PPP’s AJK chapter president Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin, Memon said, “PPP will fight for our Kashmiri brothers until the last moment.” The Sindh senior minister accused the AJK CEC of being a PML-N supporter, alleging that the elections were being rigged in favour of the federal ruling party. Referring to Sanaullah and Muqam’s press conference earlier in the day, Memon said they did not show any signs of guilt; rather, “they were proud of themselves for having stolen AJK’s mandate”. He said that PPP would not resort to bad language and ridicule the way PML-N did. Sharjeel claimed that in the Mirpur polls, PML-N candidates “stamped” ballot papers in LA-1, LA-5, LA-9, LA-11 and LA-12. He added that PPP had filed applications before the Election Commission against the alleged action but received no response. “When the entire country knows that they won the 2024 elections through a donated mandate and rigging, but they have not accepted that to date, so how would they accept the rigging in AJK?” Memon claimed. “I believe that the federal government’s last days have begun,” the PPP leader remarked. Memon said that polling in LA-27 was postponed yesterday citing rainfall, despite there being no showers on Sunday in the area. He contended that the Election Commission did not have the required capacity and could not arrange ballot materials on time. In LA-28, only seven out of 10 union councils (UCs) were equipped for balloting, according to the Sindh minister. He said elections in the other three UCs would be held on Tuesday. Memon also reiterated the PPP’s claim that acting AJK President Chaudhry Latif Akbar was attacked by PML-N workers while he was on his way to cast his vote. He added that a PPP MNA was also fired upon and suffered a bullet injury on his hand when he went to a polling station in the same constituency. “Kashmiris’ rights have been robbed for PML-N’s personal benefits,” the PPP leader said. Meanwhile, Yasin noted that at 40 polling stations, voter turnout was between 85 and 99 per cent, adding that, on average, this figure was “no more than 40 to 45pc”. Yasin also took exception to the phase-wise elections, saying that when the decision was announced, PPP workers had alerted their party chairman Bilawal that it was an “attempt to intensify rigging”. Reports of violence During the polling on Sunday, attempts were reportedly made to disrupt polling in some neighbourhoods of Muzaffarabad, but voting continued in most areas. In LA-31, Muzaffa­rabad-V (Khawra), clashes between workers of the PML-N and PPP were reported in Union Council Katkair. The PPP alleged that one of its workers, Syed Mushtaq Shah, was killed in an attack by PML-N supporters. The PML-N rejected the allegation, claiming the man suffered a cardiac arrest following a scuffle between two groups. There was no independent confirmation of either claim. PPP candidate and Legislative Assembly Speaker Akbar also wrote to the AJK chief election commissioner, alleging security lapses, firing incidents, interference in polling, prevention of polling agents from entering polling stations and denial of voting rights. He also claimed there had been an attempt on his life in which Advocate Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi was injured, and called for an investigation and legal action against those responsible. There was no immediate response from the Election Commission. Clashes between workers of the two major parties, some involving the use of firearms, were also reported from other areas, though no casualties were immediately reported. Low turnout outside AJK Outside AJK, Kashmiris voted for their candidates vying for refugee seats at polling stations set up in Chakwal, Jhelum, Rawalpindi, Islamabad, Sialkot, Narowal, Sargodha, Attock, Nawabshah, Hyderabad, Mohmand, Mansehra, Quetta, Dera Ghazi Khan, Peshawar, Sanghar, and Naushahro Feroze. Polling in these areas largely remained peaceful and recorded a low turnout. In Mohmand, not a single voter turned up at a station set up for the AJK polls. In Dera Ghazi Khan, a single registered female voter cast her ballot at the Govt Elementary School in Maumori, where a polling station had been established just for her. Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad, and Khyber Pakhtun­khwa, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab, and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad. Since early June, AJK has witnessed protests by the JAAC, which has been demanding the abolition of the 12 refugee seats in the AJK legislature. The protests have also been marred by violence . Additional input from Tariq Naqash

'Tick tock': Bilawal says PML-N's 'countdown' has begun, will hold rally in AJK's Poonch ahead of polls. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Monday reiterated his warning to the PML-N that a “countdown” for it has begun, as he declared that his party’s “movement” for people’s rights will extend to the entire country. Bilawal made the remarks in a series of video messages he shared on X, wherein he reiterated his allegations of rigging against the PML-N — his party’s ally in the Centre — during the ongoing Azad Kashmir elections. The PPP and the PML-N have been engaged in a war of words since the latter emerged in the lead in Mirpur polls on July 27. The PML-N has also won the majority of the seats in the second phase , with the PPP accusing it of rigging and other violent tactics in both phases. In one of the three clips posted on X on Monday, Bilawal affirmed that his party’s struggle for the people’s right to governance, ownership and employment will continue. “This movement will not remain restricted to the mountains of Kashmir or Gilgit-Baltistan. God-willing, I will run this movement across the entire Pakistan,” he declared. The PPP chairman added, “And my message for the friends in PML-N is just this: you can hear that voice, listen carefully, tick tock, tick tock. Your countdown has begun.” Punjab’s Information Minister Azma Bokhari even reacted to Bilawal’s statement, quipping: “Oh no, we are scared. What will happen now?” Bilawal had given a similar warning last week to the federal government, which is led by the PML-N in alliance with his own PPP. Senior leaders of his party have made similar remarks in recent days, even alleging the PML-N of rigging in the 2024 general elections, which resulted in both parties being part of the current ruling coalition. Both parties have also traded barbs over governance, political mandate and provincial performance . Last week, Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan claimed that “the powers that be” were unhappy with the ruling PML-N. In his videos today, Bilawal announced holding a jalsa in Poonch division’s Bagh town ahead of the elections set for August 10 across the division. “The PPP does not lose courage, back down or leave the field. You should be ready,” he said. The PPP chairman urged the people of Muzaffarabad’s LA-27 (Kutla) and LA-28 (Lachhrat) — where polling will be held tomorrow (August 4) after being suspended due to issues arising from bad weather — to vote for PPP candidates Bazil Naqvi and Javed Ayoub. Bilawal paid tribute to the people of Kashmir for “competing with the PML-N, its threats, rigging and bullets” in the ongoing elections. He reiterated the PPP’s claims that its party worker was killed, an MNA suffered a bullet injury, and its leader Chaudhry Latif Akbar — currently the acting AJK president — was “attacked” on Sunday during polling in Muzaffarabad. The PML-N has disputed the claim about the party worker, saying he died from a heart attack and was not part of the PPP. In one video clip, Bilawal asserted that the elections so far have not been transparent. “These were rigging elections, bullet elections, murderous elections and bloody elections,” he claimed. Addressing his supporters, he said, “Despite all this, you have secured nine seats for PPP. God-willing, I will get you back the seats stolen from you in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad.” CEC stresses law and order for polling to go ahead on all Poonch seats Separately, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal stressed the importance of law and order in Poonch for polling to proceed in all constituencies on August 10. The AJK CEC told the media today that considering the situation in Poonch division, the commission would conduct polling on August 10 in three constituencies in Bagh, one in Haveli and one in Abbaspur. However, the constituencies of Baloch and Palandri (in Sudhnoti district) were also under consideration, he said. “If we receive positive reports from there and the way people in Muzaffarabad rejected all pressures and tactics, came out of their homes and cast their votes, people in Poonch also extend the same cooperation, God-willing, we are ready to hold elections in all constituencies except for Rawalakot city and Thorar.” At the same time, he said: “Our preparation is complete for all constituencies. However, the law and order situation and the demands of the safety of voters play an important role in holding elections.” Responding to a question, he said that under the AJK constitution, the current Legislative Assembly ceases to exist after August 4. “Even if elections cannot be held in two or a few more constituencies, one cannot say that the house is not complete or those who have returned cannot take oath or perform their functions,” he explained. He said the new assembly would still take oath after the completion of the August 10 polls. For LA-27, where the election had been postponed across the constituency, he said polling will be held at all 197 polling stations tomorrow (Tuesday). Polling would be held on Tuesday from 8am to 5pm at 54 polling stations in three union councils (UCs) of LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat). Polling staff and election material could not reach these areas in time due to road blockades. At two of these polling stations, supporters of a candidate had set ballot boxes on fire. The CEC affirmed that adequate arrangements had been made to reopen the roads following bad weather. After security personnel returned from other areas, additional forces had been deployed in view of the sensitivity of these constituencies to ensure the electoral process was completed peacefully. He added that polling staff had already been dispatched to their respective stations under security escort. In view of Tuesday’s polling, the Muzaffarabad deputy commissioner has declared a public holiday across the district. AJK Election Commissioner retd Justice Ghulam Mustafa Mughal addresses the media on Aug 3, 2026. — Photo provided by Tariq Naqash Expressing regret over allegations levelled against the Election Commission, CEC Mughal said the electoral watchdog was a constitutional and autonomous institution whose responsibility was to conduct free, fair and impartial elections without favouring any party. He said it was the state’s responsibility to provide full security and assist the Election Commission. “We perform our duties in accordance with the Constitution and the law, and our conscience is clear.” Speaking about the second phase of elections held on Sunday, the AJK CEC said voter turnout in the seven constituencies stood at 53 per cent. “This was certainly a difficult election, and given the circumstances that were created, this is by no means a low turnout,” retired Justice Mughal noted. “I congratulate the people for making the right decision. They rejected the path of violence and chose the power of the vote instead — a path of positive change that will produce beneficial results.” Ruling coalition ‘safe’ even without PPP The PML-N-led federal government is said to be in a safe position even if the PPP withdraws its support to the PML-N in the National Assembly, as in the house of a total of 336 members, 169 votes are required to form the government. Presently, the NA has 333 members as three seats are vacant. Of these, the ruling alliance comprises: PML-N with 132 seats; PPP with 74; Mutahidda Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) with 22; PML-Q with five; Istehkam-i-Pakistan Party (IPP) with four; independents with four; and PML-Z, National Party (NP) and Balochistan Awami Party (BAP) with one seat each. The numbers show that even if the PPP leaves the ruling coalition, the PML-N-led alliance will have 170 seats, which is one seat more than the required number of 169 seats. On the other hand, the opposition has a total of 89 votes, with PTI (who are considered independents) having 74 seats, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-F (JUI-F) having 10 seats and one seat each held by Sunni Ittehad Council (SIC), Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) and Pashtunkhwa Milli Awami Party (PkMAP). If the PPP and the entire opposition join hands, even then they cannot topple the PML-N-led set-up, as the combined 163 members are six less than the 169 seats required to form the government. Whereas, if the PPP continues to attach itself to the ruling alliance, the alliance’s total seats will remain 244, 20 more seats than the number required for a two-thirds majority in the house to make any legislation smoothly.

Senate body slams linking members to seizure of smuggled cigarettes. ISLAMABAD: The subcommittee of the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control on Monday strongly condemned what it called a “malicious media campaign” targeting its members following the seizure of 11 trucks allegedly loaded with smuggled cigarettes on the motorway. The meeting, convened by Senator Saifullah Abro at Parliament House, was mandated to scrutinise border security mechanisms, smuggling networks, anti-narcotics controls, and tax evasion, including an estimated $1 billion attributed to the tobacco sector. The convener of the committee noted that after the July 20 meeting discussed the truck seizure, an official press release and handout were circulated the next day on TV channels targeting the committee chairman and members. The committee directed the Member of FBR to personally review the handout issued by his media wing and identify officials responsible. The FIA has also been tasked with conducting a “completely impartial, full-scale inquiry” into TV channels running target­­ed smear campaigns and submit a report. On the seizure of 11 trucks laden with smuggled cigarettes, the committee questioned jurisdiction, stating that Motorway operations fall under the Inland Revenue and not Customs. It raised alarm over “contradictory valuation figures amounting to Rs220 million and ordered owners of the transport and steel company concerned to submit a full report by Monday evening. It also questioned the legal basis of the FIR registered by Customs, noting that 11 truck drivers were arrested and produced in the court after a six-day delay. The inspector who drafted the FIR has been summoned. The Deputy Collector of Customs was directed to explain why political figures present at the site were omitted from the official reporting. Cotton production jumps 32 per cent. Textile mills have become reliant on imports amid falling cotton output.—PPI/file LAHORE: Phutti (seed-cotton) arrivals at ginning factories rose by more than 32 per cent year-on-year by July 31, driven by a sharp increase in Sindh despite a slight decline in Punjab, according to the figures released by the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA) on Monday. The PCGA fortnightly report revealed that phutti arrivals reached 785,822 bales by July 31, up 32.33pc from 593,821 bales received during the corresponding period last year. It showed that Punjab’s arrivals stood at 298,150 bales, down 1.1 per cent from a year earlier, while Sindh recorded 487,672 bales, marking a record 66.82pc increase despite recent monsoon rains. Balochistan also posted a 52.67pc rise in arrivals to 22,900 bales. Cotton Ginners Forum Chairman Ihsanul Haq pointed out a significant discrepancy between the PCGA figures and the Punjab government’s Crop Reporting Service (CRS). While the PCGA data showed phutti arrivals in Punjab at around 298,000 bales, the CRS claimed production of about 435,000 bales by July 30, roughly 32pc higher than the PCGA estimate. He said the difference warranted clarification from the relevant authorities. Sindh’s record 67pc surge by July 31 offsets Punjab decline despite rains He said the CRS figures also reflected an alarming collapse in cotton cultivation across Bahawalpur Division, where only around 17,000 bales were produced despite the region once being Pakistan’s leading cotton-growing belt. According to him, the rapid expansion of sugarcane cultivation, driven by the concentration of sugar mills in the region, has transformed the traditional cotton zone into a sugarcane belt, undermining domestic cotton production. Mr Haq warned that shrinking cotton acreage, due to increasing sugarcane sowing, was forcing the country to rely increasingly on imports of both cotton and edible oil. He urged the federal and provincial governments to restore cotton cultivation by restricting sugarcane farming in designated cotton-growing areas. Pakistan imported a record 3.482 million tonnes of edible oil worth $3.785 billion in 2025-26, compared with 3.214m tonnes valued at $3.40bn a year earlier. The PCGA report showed that textile mills purchased 704,000 bales, while exporters bought 3,400 bales, leaving 78,044 bales unsold at ginning factories. A total of 231 ginning factories were operational across the country, including 108 in Punjab and 123 in Sindh, although some units had either become partially operational or suspended operations due to financial and commercial constraints. Sanghar district alone accounted for 398,000 bales, representing 82pc of Sindh’s production and 51pc of the national total, largely because cotton sown in the province’s coastal areas during February and March had reached the market earlier than crops in other regions. Commenting on the latest arrivals, Sajid Mahmood, head of the Transfer of Technology Department at the Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan, said the early-season figures suggested a stronger start than last year, particularly in Sindh where timely sowing, harvesting and improved crop management had supported higher arrivals. However, he cautioned that August and September would provide a more reliable indication of the overall crop. He also warned that prolonged humidity and rainfall could increase the incidence of whitefly, pink bollworm and crop diseases, affecting lint quality and yields. He advised growers to ensure proper drainage, closely monitor pest populations and adopt plant protection measures in consultation with agricultural extension officials.
