Govt executes agreements with pension fund managers. • 16 companies to establish separate pension funds, ensure death and disability risk cover for employees • Centre to establish non-banking finance company to assist in implementation, monitoring of pension scheme ISLAMABAD: The government has executed agreements with 16 pension fund managers to formally operationalise the Defined Contribution Pension Fund Scheme (DCPFS) launched a year ago for public sector employees as part of major pension reforms aimed at containing the snowballing pension burden on the budget. In an announcement, the Ministry of Finance said it had executed agreements with 16 eligible pension fund managers, most of them banks and insurance companies. Around 10 of these eligible fund managers are owned or led by major commercial banks in the country. They include ABL Asset Management Company, Al Habib Asset Management, Al Meezan Investment, Faysal Asset Management, JS Investments, MCB Investment, Alfalah Asset Management, HBL Asset Management, UBL Fund Managers and NBP Fund Management, The pension fund managers led by or owned by insurance companies include EFU Life Assurance and Pak-Qatar Family Takaful. The remaining funds — Atlas Asset Man­agement, Lucky Invest­ments, National Investments and AWT Investments are owned by various business groups. Under the agreements and rules, these fund managers would set up, operate and manage conventional or Shariah-compliant funds for state employees under the federal government-defined contributory pension fund scheme in accordance with the Voluntary Pension System Rules 2005. Only these eligible pension fund managers shall be authorised to launch and manage employer pension funds for which the government will ensure annual budgetary allocation for the employer’s contribution. The agreements entail standard terms and conditions for providing systems support and electronic transfer of contributions to the pension fund’s designated bank accounts and further allocation of units to the relevant sub-funds in each employee’s pension account as per the allocation policy. The agreements also envisage a mandatory insurance plan, providing death and disability risk cover to the employees, to be arranged by these fund managers. The eligible pension fund managers will establish separate pension funds, while the government is responsible for the creation of a Non-Banking Finance Company (NBFC) to assist in implementation and monitoring of the pension fund scheme. Till such time the NBFC is established and fully operationalised, the government itself, through the finance ministry, will perform the NBFC role and establish an online portal to facilitate opening of pension accounts of employees, obtain information and data from eligible pension fund managers or otherwise communicate with the fund managers. Under the rules, employees will not withdraw any amount from the pension account before retirement is notified. Even upon reaching retirement age, the employee shall not withdraw more than 25pc of the accumulated balance in the pension account, and shall invest the remaining amount in the manner prescribed in the Voluntary Pension System Rules, 2005, for a period of at least twenty years or till his death, whichever is earlier. However, the rules allow employees to transfer pension account balance from one eligible pension fund manager to another. The government had announced pension reforms in 2024 to introduce a contributory pension fund for all government employees, including civil government and armed forces personnel. In a formal announcement in the National Assembly, the government said the contributory pension scheme would apply to all civil employees of the federal government, including civilian employees paid from defence estimates appointed on a regular basis on or after July 1, 2024. A September 2024 notification stated that the scheme would also apply to armed forces personnel appointed on or after July 1, 2025. While the civilian side of the scheme has been implemented and the government has already set aside about Rs25bn for the scheme as its initial share, the contributory pension scheme for armed forces was deferred for a year to 2026 due to concerns over their peculiar nature of duties requiring detailed review, according to earlier statements by the finance minister and secretary. Officials said the contributory pension scheme for armed forces personnel, which had been postponed two years ago, had been further delayed owing to internal departmental consultations and challenging security conditions, hindering any move that could be seen demoralising personnel. The finance ministry notified in October 2025 that federal employees would contribute 10pc of their pensionable pay to qualify for a 12pc contribution from the public exchequer under the newly formalised contributory pension fund scheme. The total contribution rate will thus be 22pc, replacing the traditional pension system for new entrants. The October notification and pension rules superseded an earlier order of August 2024, which had set the government’s contribution at 20pc. On Aug 20, 2024, the ministry initially announced the introduction of the contributory pension scheme for new entrants to the civil government and armed forces. At that time, employees were to contribute 10pc of their basic pay, while the government was to contribute 20pc. The contributory pension scheme was introduced on the advice of international lenders, notably the World Bank, to contain the rising pension liabilities, which the government had itself described as a growing fiscal risk. It does not apply to existing employees but aims to slow future growth in pension liabilities. Federal pension expenditure is estimated at Rs1.170tr for FY2026-27, including about Rs860bn for military pensions and about Rs300bn for civil employees. The pension budget had increased from Rs1.055tr in 2025-26. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

Pakistan gets a pass on new US visa bond rule. • Washington makes visa bond programme permanent; Bangladesh, Nepal among 50 countries covered, India also excluded • Visitors from listed nations face refundable deposits of up to $20,000 WASHINGTON: Pakistan is not among the 50 countries whose citizens may now be required to deposit up to $20,000 as a financial guarantee before obtaining a US visitor visa under a new programme that took effect on Aug 1. The list published in the US Federal Register does not include Pakistan. Among South Asian countries, Bangladesh and Nepal are covered by the programme, while India is not. Afghanistan and Iran are not included because the United States does not maintain normal diplomatic relations with either country. The State Department said the decision followed a review of the 2025 pilot programme, which it said significantly reduced visa overstays among travellers from participating countries and improved compliance with US immigration rules. Officials said those findings prompted Washington to make the programme permanent. According to the department, there were 45,488 overstays from these 50 countries in 2024. In the first 10 months of the pilot, the number of overstays was fewer than 50. The visa bond requirement has also resulted in a decrease in visa issuance, as some applicants appear to self-select by not paying a bond. Diplomatic sources also confirmed to Dawn that “Pakistan is not on the list of countries covered by the programme”. The programme applies to applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas from countries covered by the scheme. Under the new rules, US consular officers may require selected applicants to post a refundable bond of between $10,000 and $20,000 before issuing a visa. The regulations make permanent a visa bond pilot launched in 2025 after the US State Department concluded that it had helped reduce visa overstays. The new rules also increase the maximum bond from $15,000 to $20,000 and eliminate the previous $5,000 minimum bond available during the pilot programme. The 50 countries covered by the programme include 30 African nations as well as countries in Asia, the Caribbean and the Pacific. The bond will be refunded if the visitor complies with all visa conditions and leaves the United States before the authorised period of stay expires. Applicants who overstay or otherwise violate the terms of their visas risk forfeiting the deposit. The bond requirement does not apply automatically to all applicants from the countries covered by the programme. Instead, US consular officers will determine on a case-by-case basis whether a bond is warranted before issuing a visa. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

PCB moves IHC against orders to disclose players’ financial details. ISLAMABAD: The Pak­istan Cricket Board (PCB) has approached the Islam­abad High Court (IHC), challenging two separate orders of the Pakistan Information Commission (PIC) directing the board to disclose extensive financial, contractual and operational information relating to national cricketers, selection committee members and other PCB officials under the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017. The petitions, filed through Advocate Kashif Ali Malik, are fixed for hearing before IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar. The first petition challenges the PIC’s order of July 9, requiring the PCB to disclose its annual budgets for the financial years 2023 to 2025, along with a detailed breakdown of expenditure; policies governing the confidentiality and disclosure of such information; details of players and officials who travelled for this year’s T20 World Cup; and details of the board’s audit mechanisms and reports. The second petition relates to information concerning Pakistan’s ODI series against South Africa held at Iqbal Stadium, Faisalabad, in November 2025. Through its order, the PIC directed the PCB to provide a breakdown of revenue, expenditure and details of steps taken or proposed to upgrade Iqbal Stadium for hosting PSL Season 12. Board claims disclosure orders threaten commercial interests, privacy rights of players Since taking office in 2024, PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi has stopped publishing the board’s financial statements on the PCB website. These statements had previously detailed expenditure across all departments, including the chairman’s office. The PCB has contended that it operates in a highly competitive international sporting environment and, unlike government departments funded through the public exchequer, receives no funding from the federal government or the Consoli­dated Fund. Instead, it says its revenues are generated primarily through commercial activities, including broa­dcasting rights, sponsorship agreements, media rights, gate receipts, licensing arrangements, international cricket events and distributions from the Inte­rnational Cricket Council. In its petitions, the PCB argues that the impugned orders wrongly assume that all information sought is subject to disclosure under Section 5 of the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017, while ignoring the Act’s express exemptions protecting personal privacy, confidential contractual arrangements, commercially sensitive information and third-party interests under Section 16. It contends that the information sought extends beyond institutional expenditure to confidential contractual and personal financial information of identifiable individuals, without recognising the distinction between institutional transparency and private financial affairs. The PCB submitted that disclosure of confidential remuneration structures and contractual terms would prejudice its commercial interests and contractual negotiations. The board also sought interim relief, arguing that once confidential contractual and personal financial information entered the public domain, the resulting prejudice to its commercial interests, contractual relationships and the privacy rights of third parties would be irreversible. 144 children lost to diphtheria, measles since January in Karachi. • Deaths from vaccine-preventable diseases reported at four tertiary care city hospitals • Expert says most parents fail to ensure children receive recommended doses on time • EPI official claims cases declined this year KARACHI: At least 144 children have lost to measles and diphtheria — both vaccine-preventable infections — at four key tertiary care hospitals in the first seven months of this year, it emerged on Monday. Sources said that a total of 1,915 cases of measles with 125 mortalities have been reported at the four hospitals —Indus Hospital (IH), Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital and Research Centre (SIDH&RC), National Institute of Child Health (NICH) and Sindh Institute of Child Health and Neonatology (SICHN) — this year so far. Eighty-one cases of diphtheria were reported at SIDH&RC, eight at Indus Hospital (8) with 19 deaths. Detailed analysis of the data showed that at least 17 children have lost their lives to measles — a highly contagious viral infection — at IH with around 850 cases this year so far. In addition, a child died of diphtheria at the hospital, which has recorded at least eight of cases of the bacterial infection. At SID&RC, at least 54 children — 36 from measles and 18 from diphtheria — have died during the period between Jan 1 and July 26, 2026. The total number of measles and diphtheria cases reported at the facility was 575 and 81, respectively. While detailed data of the NICH was not available, sources at the province’s largest public-sector hospital for children shared that at least seven children have died of measles at the facility in recent weeks. “We get complicated cases after the patient has already been mismanaged at multiple health facilities. At that stage, measles has either turned into encephalitis [a dangerous swelling and inflammation of the brain] or pneumonia [the most common measles’ complication]. The former carries a significant risk of death and long-term disability,” a doctor at the NICH told Dawn on the condition of anonymity. Information gathered from SICHN showed that 484 cases of measles have been reported this year so far at the facility with 65 deaths. Role of healthcare providers Explaining why a significant number of children couldn’t get protection against diseases that could easily be prevented through vaccines available free of cost under the Expanded Programme for Immunisation (EPI), Dr Khalid Shafi of the Pakistan Paediatric Association said that the tragedy in Pakistan was that the coverage rate of vaccine doses given at birth was 90 per cent but this number declined sharply as the child grows, requiring subsequent doses of vaccines. “Unfortunately, parents get negligent and the child either gets no or partial protection against several diseases including measles, typhoid and polio,” he said, adding that around 20 to 25 per cent of the child population in the country couldn’t get timely vaccination. He pointed out that the first shot of measles under the EPI programme was given at nine months and the second (the last) one at 15 months. “If 95 per cent of our children get the two shots at the right time, we can easily control this disease as the vaccine provides herd immunity to the rest of the population. Most children in our country, however, either fail to receive any dose or get only partial protection through one dose.” To address this challenge, he said countrywide vaccination drives were launched every four years. Last year, a national level drive was launched for children aged six months to five years, who were given an additional dose of MR (measles and rubella) vaccine. “Along with the government efforts, our healthcare providers have a crucial role to help tackle the vaccination coverage gap. When an ailing child reports to them, they must ask about his or her vaccination history/status and provide proper counselling to parents, if they find any vaccine doses missing. “Having said that, parents have the prime responsibility to protect their child and they must play their part with diligence. Though there are cases with children falling sick despite getting the vaccine shots, their numbers are few and the disease intensity in such cases is mild.” EPI’s response In his response, EPI Project Director Dr Raj Kumar said cases of measles and diphtheria had declined this year in the province, especially measles which saw a 35 per cent drop. According to him, 148 cases of diphtheria with 14 deaths were reported in the province in the first seven months of 2025, while this year so far 10 deaths have been reported with 46 confirmed cases. “Last year, we had 4,626 cases of measles in the first seven months with 57 deaths in the province. This year so far, we have 3,025 cases with 59 deaths,” he said. Highlighting challenges, he said that pockets of unvaccinated children and parental negligence were primary drivers of increase in cases. “Along with that, there are myths surrounding me­­asles and parents prefer traditional remedies, keep their child at home, resulting in disease complications,” he explained, adding that the government had run vaccination campaigns to cover missed children and planning to continue this process and that an additional 970 vaccinators had been recruited to address HR shortages. The government had surveillance units and collected data from hospitals, he said. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

Politics is upon us. IT wasn’t an ordinary day by any stretch of the imagination, even though it began rather ordinarily. There was little news to interest anyone (and Kashmir was a no-no for television channels). Initially, there came fleeting news about a press conference by the head of ISPR but it wasn’t meant to be. Those who had not been invited to the event thought the news was incorrect but later it transpired that the conference had been delayed to the next day, Friday. And then came the bombshell — in Islamabad at an event hosting businessmen for a conference on the economy, business and all things complicated. Here, instead of the speeches by the men managing Pakistan’s finances (if there were any), it was Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s speech that got all the attention. It’s still not clear why he spoke there but as the conference took place at a hall located close to his office, perhaps he offered to swing by and say a few words. His speech didn’t just create headlines; it created an entire news cycle. In simple words, he confirmed in a way what the government’s worst critics have been saying — that people are in pain and the government hasn’t been able to provide them with any relief. He put it even more bluntly. He spoke of the ‘system’ (the entire country — not just the one in Sindh) having collapsed. Not collapsing but collapsed. He said it wasn’t possible to deliver regardless of how hard the prime minister worked and how many long hours he put in. He referenced recent events in India , saying that if the ‘cockroaches’ (youth) got together, they would overthrow it all. But more intriguingly, he also made it clear that giving people a few thousand rupees or a laptop wasn’t enough. This was clearly a reference to the various schemes launched by the PML-N as well as the Benazir Income Support Programme, which is seen as the PPP’s baby. He proposed a solution by arguing the country needed more provinces or administrative units so that governance could be delivered at the doorstep. The next day, the DG ISPR reinforced this proposal . The interior minister’s indictment of the present government will not be forgotten easily. While his solution or proposal took no one by surprise, his criticism of the set-up did. After all, most of us are aware that there is much discussion behind closed doors on the need to revisit the NFC as well as the notion of devolution (which would assist the people as well as weaken the dynasty-controlled fiefdoms at the provincial level). However, Naqvi’s indictment of the present government will not be forgotten easily — for now, all those who had been waxing lyrical about the work done by Maryam Nawaz in Punjab or by Shehbaz Sharif at the centre will find it hard to argue that the party has delivered and won over the people. Interestingly, his remarks, which were a damning indictment of the current set-up, were initially met with silence. It took nearly a day before the reaction came from the PPP and PML-N whose public representatives are usually quick to hold media talks every day on any hint of criticism. But to contradict the interior minister, and one who is said to be very close to the highest in the establishment, is surely above the pay grade of those put in charge of information ministries. Still, the senior tiers were called to report for duty . In Sindh, the chief minister himself pooh-poohed the suggestion, while from the PML-N Rana Sanaullah was the first to fire back. Since then, others too have joined the fray, but most of the criticism focuses on Naqvi and not those who back him. There was also news of a family gathering at Jati Umrah in Lahore. Not much emerged from it other than some vloggers thundering about Nawaz Sharif having been woken up from his slumber — news that somehow didn’t get traction unlike Naqvi’s speech. Perhaps it is because the news is limited to a few who are relying on sources or because no one really believes the family is in a position to push back. The silence from the PPP heads is equally noticeable. In the meantime, the lower tiers might continue to thunder, though it is hard to believe Mohsin Naqvi will now respond to these allegations. But what now seems inevitable is another amendment to the Constitution, even if there is little clarity on what it will bring. New provinces and other wholesale changes (for it would mean reconfiguring the Senate)? Or simply a strong local government system with some federal areas? Or will it begin with easing the provisions for creating new provinces? Or a change in the NFC? Nothing is clear but the path ahead seems to lead to parliament. That Ahsan Bhoon was also present at the event where Naqvi spoke also indicates this. But while the powers that be have perhaps made their intentions clear, the silence from the parties means they are still to put together a strategy. Will they simply try to win over some concessions as they did during the previous two amendments? Will they drive a hard bargain? Or is the time and space for compromises over? The details are as above my pay grade as they are beyond the ability and position of Azma Bokhari or Atta Tarrar to respond to Naqvi. So as the hackneyed phrase goes, let’s wait and watch. However, it might just be safe to say that the amendment will not sail through without hiccups. It would mean a weakening of both the parties vis-à-vis the provincial governments, politically as well as in terms of patronage. For instance, the PPP will lose its political raison d’être; for Maryam Nawaz, the position of chief minister might lose its lustre, increasing the competition for the position in Islamabad. The initial instinct therefore will be to bargain and get something in return, if they decide not to push back. In other words, the hybrid system is now set for a new tug of war, which may leave some, if not all, of the stakeholders a little worse for wear. The writer is a journalist. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

Capital Development Authority moves for early start of work on cricket stadium. ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Monday held a consultative meeting for the early start of work on the first ever cricket stadium in the capital. In this regard, the consultant was directed to check at the earliest if construction rates presented by the contractor were reasonable. As per CDA’s plan, the stadium is going to be constructed near D-12 at the foothills of Margallas in Zone III. According to the CDA, it will be a replica of Dubai International Stadium with the capacity of 35000 spectators. Consultant directed to check if rates presented by contractor are reasonable Sources said the CDA’ member environment Abdullah Khurram Niazi chaired a meeting which was attended by the consultant and contractor and relevant officials of the civic agency. The CDA has already opened financial bids and a Joint Venture of Habib Construction Service and ZKB-EA has submitted the lowest bid of Rs8.9 billion for the structure work, including a three-kilometre road network. According to PC-I, the estimated cost of the project is Rs11.9 billion. Under the contract, the total covered area is over 600,000 square feet. Sources said during the meeting, Bills of Quantities (BOQ), scope of the work and other breakdown of the project were discussed and the consultant was directed to complete the process of reasonability of rates so that CDA could issue work orders. The area where the stadium is going to be constructed is outside of Maraglla Hills National Park, but falls in Zone III, where according to clause 4(3)(b) of the ICT Zoning Regulations 1992, no change in land use is permissible except projects related to recreation, conservation and preservation. Officials said the cricket stadium project falls in the category of recreation. Asked about the construction of hotels and commercial areas attached to the project, the CDA officials said former chairman Mohammad Ali Randhawa had sent a summary to the federal cabinet seeking permission for hotels and commercial areas. They said the Prime Minister Office had referred back the summary with some questions and CDA recently resent the same with required information. Zone III’s status Officials said the cricket stadium was part of the Olympic Village site of 175 acres, where the CDA had planned several sports facilities including hotels. Out of it, almost 50 acres will be used for the stadium project. The CDA board in its meeting held on November 21, 2025 had decided that a hotel should also be constructed in the area for accommodation of players. Subsequently, the then chairman CDA moved a summary seeking permission of the federal cabinet for a hotel and a commercial strip at the proposed Olympic Village. In the year 2022, the CDA board had decided that private areas, including Shah Allah Ditta and other villages of Zone III, should be made part of the nearest Zone I and the area of Bhara Kau should be made part of Zone IV for regulating construction. But the matter could not be taken up by the government. As per the original master plan, these areas were shown as green. Therefore, if the CDA acquires land in these areas, it will have to leave it for greenery purpose. “Neither the CDA is acquiring this area nor regulating construction, as a result of which unauthorised construction has been taking place. The issue of this zone should be decided for good,” said an official source. Meanwhile, the government is showing no interest in resolving the issue of the public in the said unacquired villages of Zone III. However, both the CDA and the government have been showing their intent for construction in Zone III. Sources said that a few years ago the CDA itself had earmarked land in Zone III for the construction of a special economic zone near Park Road. Last month, the CDA board decided to auction four kanals near the sports complex for motel/hotel project subject to approval of the federal government. The four kanals is surrendered by Islamabad Club and in a surprising move the CDA wants to auction it for a hotel project, said the sources. When contacted, CDA spokesperson Shahid Kiani said Zone III and Margalla Hills National Park were different entities. “As far as cricket stadium project is concerned, being recreational project, it is permissible use in Zone III and approved by CDA board. While, for hotel and commercial components of stadium project, we have not proceeded yet on these two components. Fate of these two components will be decided by federal government, which is a competent forum,” he said. About a new hotel site in Zone III near sports complex, he said: “Yes, this proposal is under consideration, but no final decision is made yet. There is no issue of construction of motel in said area with approval of federal government as several motels are already existed in said locality, particularly at Rawal Dam Chowk,” he said. When asked about public suffering, he said: “During the last four years, the issue of public of Zone III was taken up by CDA with federal government. As far as special economic zone in Zone III is concerned, the land for economic zone was taken from NIH and federal government okayed this site, therefore, there is no illegality involved,” he said. Over-interpreting the youth. COCKROACH Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke revealed a crucial fact about himself to Newslaundry ’s Manisha Pande. He said he had seen Shahrukh Khan’s 2002 movie Swades (‘My country’) many times over since he was a child and he finds it inspirational. So, I too switched on YouTube and saw it to the extent one could. The story is about an Indian engineer at Nasa who misses home and goes on a visit to meet the lady who raised him upon his parents’ death in a car accident. The journey takes him to a village facing chronic power outages and where he also meets Kaveri Amma’s pretty ward Gita who is struggling to run a village school. So, the hero, while living out of a caravan trailer, builds a water reservoir from a tiny stream seeping from a rocky slope to ply a turbine he has assembled. The villagers get their steady power, leaving the hero to canvass support for the underprivileged children to join the struggling school. They do so by defying entrenched caste- and poverty-related odds. The turbine event comes across as a band-aid for a country that has handed early dreams of affordable and universal healthcare to private buccaneers. The state-run National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) where corruption is rampant — which triggered Dipke’s Cockroach campaign — produces 137,000 doctors against 20 million applicants. Many who succeed go abroad to follow their dreams. The phenomenon was seen as brain drain during the early years of India’s independence and there’s a news clip of Nehru on a US visit urging Indian professionals there to return home. Dipke may have picked up the cue, but many others have returned to India over the years to work for the country’s progress. The US-born human rights lawyer Sudha Bharadwaj was jailed for working among Chhattisgarh’s tribespeople to empower them with legal advice and moral support. Bharadwaj, currently out on stiff bail conditions, exchanged her American passport for Indian citizenship. She was arrested along with several young activists in 2020 for the crime of organising the Dalits and tribespeople to challenge the injustices they endured with the state’s connivance. Rev Stan Swamy was an Indian Jesuit priest and tribal rights activist, the oldest person to be accused of terrorism in India. He died in a Mumbai prison at 83, a year after his arrest. Dipke’s movement faces inevitable challenges ahead. Ground-breaking political changes are seldom if ever a clean shot. Dipke may have seen Richard Attenborough’s award-winning movie Gandhi. Did he notice that B.R. Ambedkar or Bhagat Singh didn’t even get a walk-on part in the movie? That Ambedkar and Bhagat Singh featured in the Cockroach protests was reassuring. They had a well-grounded prognosis about what ailed Indian society. Ambedkar, together with Periyar and M.G. Ranade had forcefully argued that social transformation must precede or accompany political freedom, famously maintaining that political independence without social equality was incomplete or a ‘lie’. Umar Khalid , Sharjeel Imam and Surendra Gadling are among the current crop of youth jailed for holding the torch passed on by an amazing generation of leaders. Dipke’s movement faces inevitable challenges ahead. Ground-breaking political changes are seldom if ever a clean shot. It’s almost inevitable that there’s a Trotsky lurking to challenge Stalin in a leftist upheaval, or an Ernst Rohm paying dearly for over-interpreting his Fuhrer’s bloodlust. Likewise, leading the French Revolution, Robespierre sought to cleanse the leadership of opportunists. They ganged up to guillotine him instead. Closer to home, Z.A. Bhutto was barely finished with Ayub Khan’s military rule when he waded into a far more momentous challenge from an estranged kindred spirit, a democrat this time in faraway Dhaka. Indira Gandhi sought a clean break from corporate-feudal satraps within the Congress and garnered the left’s support against avaricious private bankers and assorted British-era princes. Then she was nudged by communal bigots still lurking in her party into a needless feud with the minority Sikhs, a grievous error that would eventually lay her low. Rajiv Gandhi sought to lead India into a perfectly viable technology-savvy 21st century. He ended up balancing the party’s advice that thrust him between Hindu and Muslim communalists, one seeking to turn mythology into history, the other bent on stealing small change from a female divorcee. Two earth-shaking upheavals in the 20th century nicely frame the context and reality of the youth-led Cockroach movement. The movement has already forced Narendra Modi’s education minister’s humiliating exit , rattling the bones of the faux muscular religio-fascist rulers. But what lies in store ahead for the lot when the exigencies of politics serve up crucial state polls next year in Uttar Pradesh and Punjab? Politicians would want to harness their energy to purposes that can neither be ignored nor trifled with. The two important examples to better understand the Cockroach phenomenon perhaps rest in movements that led to India’s 1947 independence from Britain and Iran’s 1979 freedom from American control of the country. The landmark events occurred barely 32 years apart. The Indian movement was set into motion in 1885 by professional ornithologist A.O. Hume. The Indian National Congress remained an elitist body until Gandhi turned it into a mass movement in 1920. It brought together a cornucopia of contradictions. Bhagat Singh and Lal Lajpat Rai were opposed to Gandhi’s nonviolence. While one was a votary of scientific socialism, the other was a staunch Hindu revivalist. The Iranian Revolution was similarly led by competing groups of diverse ideological origins. The spine belonged to the experienced pro-Soviet Tudeh Party. The street craft was shored up by the Maoist Mujahideen-i-Khalq, but the masses were directed by highly politically savvy and well-read clergy. After the overthrow of the Shah, the clergy took charge. They used the CIA’s files to decimate the Tudeh and uproot the MeK. Given these proven propensities, would Dipke’s worldview remain true to the promise of the dreams Bhagat Singh and Ambedkar dreamt for India? The writer is Dawn’s correspondent in Delhi. jawednaqvi@gmail.com Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

Crocodile rescued from flood-hit area in Ferozewala. LAHORE: Wildlife rangers have rescued a crocodile from the flood-hit area of Massan Kallar near Kot Abdul Malik in Ferozewala tehsil, safely relocating it to Gatwala breeding centre in Faisalabad. According to officials, after reports surfacing on social media about the presence of a crocodile in the flood-affected area of Massan Kallar, Central Zone Additional Chief Wildlife Ranger Mudassir Hassan directed Lahore Deputy Chief Wildlife Ranger Sakhi MuhammadJoiya to ensure continuous monitoring in the area. Accordingly, wildlife rangers teams conducted continuous monitoring in the area, tracing and safely rescuing the crocodile in a highly professional way. Officials say that the crocodile, which may have swept to the area in floodwaters, has been transported to Gatwala Wildlife Breeding Centre in Faisalabad, where it will undergo necessary medical examination and specialised care. After the safe rescue of the crocodile, area residents took a sigh of relief and appreciated the wildlife department’s timely action. The wildlife officials advised the public that in the event of any such situation in the future, they should immediately inform the department on its helpline, 1107, so that timely action can be taken to protect people from harm. Citizens were also strictly warned against handling such wild animals themselves. Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

No arrest made so far in MQM-P office violence in Karachi, police say. KARACHI: Police have yet to register a case and make arrests regarding a clash between two groups of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan at their party headquarters in Bahadurabad, in which a man suffered bullet wounds. On Sunday evening, police said that supporters of the Mustafa Kamal-Anis Qaimkhani group had allegedly beaten and thrown out their opponents, belonging to the Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui group, from the party headquarters. The police said heavy firing was reported from inside and outside the party office and a man, identified as Amir Ali, suffered bullet wounds. While electronic media aired news of the arrest of several workers belonging to both groups, a senior police officer told Dawn that no one has so far been formally arrested and a case is yet to be registered. The official said that the contents of the FIR had been prepared, but the police were “waiting for higher authorities to proceed further legally”. The official also denied that the Bahadurabad headquarters of the MQM-P had been sealed. He said police patrolling and deployment had been intensified to provide a sense of protection to residents, who were quite afraid following the clash and heavy firing at the MQM-P headquarters. The coffins come free here with the story. If you are new to journalism, you might need a coffin. Tell us, so we can send it to you in advance. These lines were conveyed to a reporter who could say he was from Kalat. Two phone calls came from numbers he didn’t recognise a year ago. The reporter used to cover human rights protests. He told people at work about the threats and they recommended he go to the police and file a formal complaint. Trying to be a journalist in Balochistan is one thing, having an active death wish is another. The Kalat reporter didn’t want to become Abdul Latif Baloch who had worked for daily Intekhab and Aaj TV until he was permanently stopped from working and breathing, in Mashkey, Awaran on May 24, 2025. Some men had come to get Abdul Latif at home but he had not wanted to go with them. It was the middle of the night. His wife and two daughters didn’t want him to go either because in February, Latif’s son, Saif, was similarly taken. His body was found on March 26. Four of the men decided to use their AK-47s to settle the matter. If you try to get an update on the investigation, please know that the Mashkey Police Station has no official phone number. Latif’s murder FIR has not been filed yet. Even if it was, there are no records at the station because it was set on fire once. Shahid Rind, an Aide to the Chief Minister of Balochistan, was asked about Latif’s case, but he did not respond. Forty-two journalists have been killed in Balochistan since 2008, according to the Balochistan Union of Journalists. Those who did not make it to that list will tell you how hard some people tried to put them on it. By that count, at least 42 killers are on the loose. There have never been any convictions. At least six district reporters declined to be interviewed for this story, citing security concerns, while several others agreed to speak only anonymously. Why are Baloch journalists so sought-after? After Quetta, it is Khuzdar which is home to the second largest number of graves of journalists (10 since 2006, including the three presidents of the press club, after which it was shut for four years). Every type of person, group, entity, organisation, government and law-and-order body that you can think of is heavily invested in the quality of the freedom of press here. One solution to maintaining the quality of the freedom of the press has been recommended by the union. It would like journalism to be classified as a proper career protected by the State with a Journalists Protection Bill, Balochistan, like the ones elsewhere in Pakistan. They talk about welfare and insurance and hostile environment training. In February, CM’s Aide Shahid Rind had told the Quetta Press Club that the government was ready to take up the bill and discuss it with all stakeholders (see above). The union’s president hopes he will live to report that it passed this year. The beat Most of the reporters in the districts know what is considered a dangerous story. What isn’t always understood, until it’s too late, is that reporting on construction materials, or a batch of leaked exam papers, can carry the same cost. The good news is, however, that journalists have learnt how to work safely. They stick to government handouts and press releases. But the more experienced ones will tell you that you should still check because even reporting on information that appeared in a press release is still no guarantee. A freelance journalist now based in Islamabad, Ayaz Bazai, was being hunted by a private militia over a vlog he published on the mass grave of Tutak, Khuzdar. Trump's Board of Peace reassures Israel after Tel Aviv's objections on Gaza pullout. US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace on Monday assured Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza would only begin after Hamas’s complete disarmament , following his objections. Two members of Netanyahu’s security cabinet had urged a vote to tear up the deal championed by Trump after the board released a text that called for Israel to begin a phased withdrawal. Netanyahu’s office said it had raised concerns to the United States, after Trump on Friday hailed as a “major milestone” an agreement by Hamas to hand over weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing committee. Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza under the Board of Peace, met with Netanyahu on Monday for what he acknowledged was difficult work. But the board said it had reached a “common understanding of the shared objectives” with Israel. Israel’s withdrawal beyond the Yellow Line, which demarcates the area in which Hamas still has control, “will take place only once decommissioning [of weapons] is complete, as Hamas committed to the mediators”, the board said on X. Even if Israel withdraws under the plan, it would maintain control of much of Gaza under a Trump-led October ceasefire. Hamas said late on Monday that it was adhering to “what was agreed upon regarding the implementation of the second phase of the ceasefire agreement, including the commitments of all parties”. The group was “awaiting a clear and official response” from Mladenov and the mediators on what was agreed upon, according to the statement posted on Telegram. Trump-Netanyahu gap Israel had objected to the board’s Thursday text that called for a phased withdrawal within the territory and the immediate cessation of Israeli strikes in Gaza. “Israel has conveyed its comments and concerns on the proposed framework to our American counterparts. The version that has been made public does not reflect Israel’s positions,” Doron Spielman, spokesman for the prime minister’s office, told AFP ahead of the Mladenov meeting. Far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich had said that the text was “completely different” to the one presented to Netanyahu’s security cabinet and, along with a colleague, had demanded that the cabinet “immediately” hold a new vote on the Gaza plan. Trump had earlier said that Israel was “very happy” about the disarmament announcement by Hamas. It was the latest sign of disconnect between Trump and Netanyahu, who faces a tough re-election fight in October and has heavily promoted his relationship with the US leader, whom he met again in Washington last week. Backtracking on announcement Trump and Netanyahu have also been at loggerheads on Iran, with Israel sceptical of his attempts at diplomacy to end the war the two countries launched in late February. Israeli President Isaac Herzog, who holds a largely ceremonial role, offered a more upbeat take on Trump’s Gaza efforts, saying the latest development marked “a very positive step with the clear caveat and undertaking that Hamas must be disarmed”. Mohammad Dahlan, a senior Palestinian political figure who has played a key role in the Gaza plan, said after the Board of Peace roadmap that he had spoken to Trump’s son-in-law and aide Jared Kushner, who told him that Israel would end strikes in Gaza effective on Sunday. But he quickly revised his social media post, instead saying that Kushner was “working with the Israeli side to halt the attacks” in Gaza. He later accused Netanyahu of working “to obstruct the most promising opportunity to begin ending this war”. On Monday evening, an Israeli strike on a vehicle west of Gaza City killed two Palestinians and injured several others, according to Mahmoud Bassal, a spokesperson for the civil defence rescue service. The Israeli military told AFP it targeted two fighters in the strike. On Sunday, Israeli attacks killed 19 Palestinians, including women and children, according to the civil defence. Qatar, Egypt and Turkey, which are mediating the truce in Gaza, late on Monday criticised Israel after renewed strikes in the Palestinian territory. They strongly condemned what they said were “ongoing Israeli violations in the Gaza Strip, particularly the targeting of health facilities and infrastructure, and the casualties among civilians, including women and children”.

PCB appoints South Africa's Michael Smith as batting coach for Pakistan men's cricket team. Former South African cricketer Michael Smith has been appointed as the batting coach of the Pakistan men’s cricket team for two years, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced on Tuesday. According to a press release issued by the PCB, the “46-year-old will work with the team across both red-ball and white-ball formats”. He will join the Pakistan team ahead of the three-match Test series against England, commencing on Aug 19, the press release stated. Elaborating on Smith’s experience, the press release stated that he had featured in 89 first-class matches, 72 List-A matches and 16 T20 matches between 2003 and 2013. “The right-handed batter scored 7,029 runs across the three formats, including nine centuries and 40 half-centuries,” the PCB said. Smith, who holds a Level 4 coaching qualification, has served on the coaching staffs of three HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchises — Islamabad United, Karachi Kings and Multan Sultans, it added The press release further stated that he has also worked as a batting coach with Australian franchise Hobart Hurricanes and Cricket Tasmani. As a coaching consultant, Smith has worked with South Africa’s KZN Inland and Eastern Province, the press release added. Prior to Smith’s appointment, former Test batter Asad Shafiq was appointed as Pakistan’s interim batting coach in April 2026 for the Bangladesh Test series. Shafiq is currently also accompanying the Pakistan team for its two-match Test series in the West Indies. Additional input from Mohammad Yaqoob

Hundreds of migrant children are stranded in Spain's Ceuta after mass crossing. CEUTA, Spain (AP) — The teenage girl made it through the waves to Spanish territory. Her little brother did not, drowning in the Mediterranean, while their mother disappeared in the chaos when tens of thousands of people surged through the breakwater, trying to leave Morocco behind. The tragic story of a 17-year-old from Tangier is representative of the plight of many of the more than 800 minors who four days after the collective push by migrants into Ceuta face a scary present and an uncertain future. She told an Associated Press photojournalist how she and her family joined the massive crowd that tried to swim around a border fence to reach the Spanish territory on Thursday. Like many, she said they did so seeking better opportunities. The AP is withholding her identity because she is a minor in a vulnerable situation. She described how she saw Spanish police pull the body of her 8-year-old brother from the water. She made it to the shore but became separated from her mother, and has spent the last four days on her own. She said some locals gave her food and some clothing, with one woman taking her into her home so she could bathe. She then went to a center for youths run by the government for some help, but found it was full. “I saw people stepping on the dead,” she said through a translator since she doesn't speak Spanish. “Now we are children begging on the street.” She is one of some 860 minors who remained in Ceuta on Monday after crossing over, according to local officials. AP journalists saw other minors asking for food. Those minors now make up a large part of the 3,000-5,000 migrants who have avoided expulsion from Ceuta of the original 60,000 who came across. Spanish authorities confirmed 72 people died, mostly in the water, during the crossing. Morocco reported 11 deaths which are not included in the Spanish total, the Spanish interior ministry said. Minors must be cared for under Spanish law Spanish law says that adult migrants can apply for asylum. If rejected, they will face expulsion procedures. The bar is normally very high for Moroccans to be granted humanitarian protection. Migrant minors who are unaccompanied by adults, however, are supposed to be granted protection and taken care of by Spanish authorities. An AP journalist witnessed Spanish soldiers escorting an unaccompanied Moroccan boy who was crying and begging not to be sent back to Morocco. A few meters before reaching the border, and due to pressure from local residents who insisted he was a minor, as well as the presence of the media, a lieutenant colonel in the Spanish Army stopped the repatriation and transferred the boy to the Spanish Civil Guard. Most of the Moroccan adults have either voluntarily gone home or were pushed back by Spanish police. Among those who remain in Ceuta are significant numbers of people from other countries, including Sudanese fleeing their war-torn country, Palestinians from Gaza and Afghans, as well as people from several African nations. The city’s migrant center with a capacity for 600 people is completely full. Food is scarce among the migrants, according to reporting by AP journalists. “The strategy is that hunger, thirst and exhaustion force these people to finally decide to voluntarily return to Morocco,” said local migration activist Ramsés Mohamed Azumik of Asociación Elín. Many migrants sleep or rest on the beach or hills surrounding the speck of Spain. In the hazy distance, mainland Europe, their ultimate goal, lies across the sea.

DTI Undersecretary Allan Gepty told reporters last Monday, Aug. 3, that the Philippines and Canada had a “very successful” round of negotiations in Ottawa, the Canadian capital, last week. “In terms of progress that was achieved, it was very substantive. So, I can say that we’re still on track,” he said. Gepty said several chapters of the FTA were finalized during the latest round. The talks also focused largely on market access for trade in goods. Since negotiations for the trade pact were launched in October last year, the Philippines and Canada have completed three rounds of talks. The first negotiating round was held in February this year in Pasay City, followed by the second round in April in Mandaluyong City. Like the third round, the next round of negotiations in September will also be held in Ottawa. Gepty said he is hopeful that the Philippines and Canada can finalize all text-based negotiations and market access commitments during the fourth round. Asked whether the next round of talks would be the last, Gepty said it would still depend on the progress made in the remaining chapters of the FTA. Still, he said the target remains to conclude negotiations within the year. During a public consultation last month, Gepty said the government would do its best to conclude negotiations with Canada in November. Once signed, the FTA with Canada will be the Philippines’ first with a North American country. DTI data showed that bilateral merchandise trade between the two countries reached $2.15 billion in 2025, with Canada ranking as the Philippines’ 16th-largest trading partner among 229 economies. Philippine exports to Canada reached $1.31 billion last year, led by unrefined copper, copper anodes, and ignition wiring sets. Imports from Canada totaled $840 million, consisting mainly of wheat, meslin, wood, and copper ores and concentrates. Gepty said the trade surplus demonstrates that there are still many opportunities for Philippine exporters to expand their presence in the Canadian market through improved market access under the FTA. In addition, the DTI official said the trade pact could also help attract new investments into the country. Data from the Canadian Embassy showed that Canadian investment in the Philippines reached $1.7 billion last year, while Philippine investment in Canada stood at $51 million.

Dating app meetup ends in iPhone 17 Pro theft at Manila gas station. A content creator was robbed of his iPhone 17 Pro at a Manila gas station by a man he met through a dating app. The victim, who used the alias “Fifi,” said the incident happened on July 2 at around 2 a.m., just two days after he met and began talking to the suspect on Tinder. In a TikTok post, the victim said the suspect picked him up on a motorcycle from his condo and claimed to be a student-athlete from La Salle. He appeared well-presented, prompting the victim to agree to the meetup. While on the way to a coffee shop along Legarda Street, the suspect asked him to open a navigation app, saying he was unfamiliar with the route. The phone was placed on the motorcycle holder, where the suspect allegedly locked it repeatedly, prompting the victim to enter his passcode several times. The victim later realized the suspect may have been memorizing the passcode. The suspect then stopped at a gas station, saying he would refuel. As the victim got off, the rider suddenly sped away, taking the phone. The device had been with the victim for only six months and was not yet fully paid, he said, adding that he immediately alerted his banks and e-wallets due to possible access. “Nanakaw sa akin yung iPhone 17 Pro ko dahil nakipagkita ako sa guy na nakilala ko lang sa dating app (My iPhone 17 Pro was stolen after I met up with a guy I only knew from a dating app),” he said in his video, which he shared to warn others about meeting strangers online. Gas station workers assisted the victim after the incident, and he later sought help from local authorities. After posting his experience, the victim said that around 23 individuals reached out, claiming they had encountered the same suspect since 2022 and that the suspect had engaged in similar schemes ranging from theft to acts of lasciviousness. On July 31, police received a tip that placed the suspect in Makati, prompting them to act. The Manila Police District confirmed the suspect had an existing warrant of arrest for acts of lasciviousness in Imus, Cavite, as well as another for theft in Makati. Authorities tracked him to a call center where he worked and arrested him as he left the building. Following Fifi's post, police encouraged other possible victims to come forward and file complaints, saying the incident should serve as a cautionary tale and help authorities build stronger cases against repeat offenders.

World championship dreams spark IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu showdown. Beyond the battle for podium finishes, the IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu presented by Megaworld on Aug. 9 in Mactan, Cebu offers something even bigger for local triathletes – a coveted opportunity to earn a place in one of endurance sports' most prestigious events. Serving as an official qualifying race for the 2027 IRONMAN 70.3 World Championship, the Cebu staging gives Filipino age-group athletes the rare privilege of chasing world championship berths on home soil while experiencing the atmosphere, organization and level of competition that define a premier global triathlon event. The race, to be held at the Mactan Newtown, will challenge competitors with the iconic 1.9-km swim, 90-km bike and 21.1-km run across a demanding world-class course that has become a favorite among local and international participants alike. A total of 50 age-group qualifying slots will be up for grabs, including 25 reserved for women as part of IRONMAN's continued commitment to promoting gender equality and increasing female participation in the sport, according to the organizing Sunrise Events, Inc. Those who secure qualification will earn the right to compete in the 2027 IRONMAN 70.3 World Championship scheduled on Aug. 28-29, 2027 in Chattanooga, Tennessee, a scenic city renowned for its outdoor attractions, Civil War heritage and iconic landmarks such as the Tennessee Aquarium, Lookout Mountain and the Walnut Street Bridge. The Lapu-Lapu race joins an elite roster of qualifying events worldwide, alongside races in Sweden, France, Canada, the United Kingdom, Luxembourg, Spain, Poland, Ecuador, Malaysia, Brazil, Germany, Estonia and Austria, among others, underscoring Cebu's stature as one of the sport's premier destinations. This year's staging also marks the 12th anniversary of the IRONMAN 70.3 in Cebu, a milestone that highlights the event's longevity and growing stature within the global IRONMAN circuit. Over the past decade, the race has consistently attracted elite professionals and thousands of age-group competitors while earning a reputation for world-class organization and race execution. More than 1,000 athletes from 48 countries are competing in this year's edition, further cementing the event's international appeal. Headlining the professional field are 2024 champion and Olympic bronze medalist Henri Schoeman of South Africa and Australian Olympian Natalie Van Coevorden, both expected to spearhead another highly competitive elite race. Still, much of the spotlight will be on the age-group competition, where local triathletes will battle not only for division honors but also for the chance to represent the Philippines on the world stage. Under the qualification system, every male and female age-group champion automatically earns a guaranteed slot to the world championship. Should the winner decline, the berth rolls down to the second-place finisher and then to third place within the same age group. For Filipino triathletes, the Aug. 9 race presents more than another stop on the racing calendar. It is an opportunity to test themselves against some of the sport's best, compete in a world-class race environment without leaving the country, and possibly turn a strong performance in Cebu into a ticket to the biggest stage in long-course triathlon.

Lacson says Taguig ghost project probe opens ‘cauldron of worms’; seeks forfeiture of reclaimed land in favor of government. Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano may end up drowning in truth after all as Sen. Panfilo “Ping” Lacson and his team has uncovered a “cauldron of worms” involving ghost slope projection projects in Taguig City, the minority leader’s political bailiwick. Lacson said this includes harassment tactics employed by the senator, and illegal reclamation of portions of Laguna Lake that he said should be forfeited in favor of the government. According to Lacson, his team’s finding was validated by officials of the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA) officials after a meeting on Monday evening. The PRA is under the Office of the President. "'MALULUNOD SA KATOTOHAHAN' ... Our Taguig City case study has opened a 'cauldron of worms' after my meeting with Philippine Reclamation Authority officials last night - from ghost slope protection projects to illegally reclaimed tracts of land covering Laguna Lake," he said on X . "Aside from the PRA and the Ombudsman, we will closely coordinate with the DPWH central office, LLDA and other concerned agencies not only to jail the crooks behind these grossly anomalous and patently illegal activities but also forfeit the already reclaimed Lakeshore areas in favor of the national government. There is no turning back!" he added. https://x.com/iampinglacson/status/2084432123054932127 The former national police chief said PRA officials confirmed the harassment tactics employed by Cayetano during budget deliberations last November 2025, when the budget for the Office of the President was taken up for plenary debates. "The same officials, likewise, disclosed physical intimidation when they conducted on site inspection along C6 in the Lakeshore area where the illegal reclamation activities are taking place," he said. Last weekend, Lacson cited evidence linking the former Senate President to reclamation projects along Taguig’s lakeshore development that lacked the required permits from agencies including the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR).The projects were funded using appropriations in the national budget that were meant for slope protection projects. At the time, the resource persons who knew about this were harassed and intimidated, especially during committee hearings, he said.Also last week, Lacson and his team turned over to the Office of the Ombudsman the evidence they gathered from at least five case studies on anomalous infrastructure projects in Taguig City. According to Lacson, the evidence points to Cayetano virtually controlling Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) operations and other related activities in Taguig City, with district engineers being replaced if they acted without his approval. Lacson also bared a possible 33-percent kickback structure in infrastructure projects in Taguig City.

Couple robbed while sheltering from rain in Rizal. Rizal police on Tuesday, Aug. 4, said they are pursuing four armed men who allegedly robbed a couple of their motorcycle, mobile phones, and wallet while the victims were taking shelter from the rain in Taytay. The Taytay Municipal Police Station reported that the incident occurred on July 29 but was only brought to their attention on Monday, Aug. 3. According to the initial investigation, the 21-year-old victim and his girlfriend were waiting for the rain to stop in front of a motorcycle parts and accessories shop on Ortigas Avenue Extension in Barangay Dolores, Taytay, at around 1 a.m. Police said four unidentified men riding two motorcycles suddenly arrived, dismounted, and declared a holdup while pointing a firearm and a bladed weapon at the victims. The suspects then forcibly took the victims’ motorcycle, a Yamaha Mio Aerox S BRW5 with plate number D828IK, before fleeing toward Kaytikling. They also seized the victims’ mobile phones and a wallet. Authorities said available CCTV footage did not capture the holdup itself but showed the suspects arriving on two motorcycles. The investigation is ongoing to identify and arrest the suspects.

Wong claims 2 titles in San Pablo juniors netfest. Francine Wong emerged as the tournament's lone double champion, capturing the girls’ 14- and 16-and-under singles titles to headline the San Pablo City Juniors Age Group Championships at the 7 Lakes Tennis Club courts in Laguna last Sunday, July 2. The Cagayan de Oro standout displayed grit and versatility in claiming her two crowns. She rallied from a set down to outlast Anica Palacio, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1, in the girls’ 14-and-U finals before producing a far more dominant performance in the 16-and-U championship, overpowering Claire Alcala, 6-3, 6-0. Wong’s two-title sweep highlighted the four-division Group 2 tournament, which kicked off the Luzon swing of the nationwide Palawan Junior Series after the successful staging of the Mindanao and Visayas swings. Rafael Monte de Ramos likewise turned in an impressive campaign, ruling the boys’ 18-and-U division after conceding only seven games in his first three matches before blanking Bien Tulop, 6-0, 6-0, in the championship match. The Lipa City, Batangas ace, however, fell short of a second singles title after retiring while trailing Aljhon Rombawon, 7-5, 4-0, in the boys’ 16-and-U semifinals. Rombawon went on to complete his own comeback story, recovering from a set down to defeat Nicholas Andal, 2-6, 6-3, 6-1, for the crown. Monte de Ramos, however, shared the tournament MVP honors with Wong. Joining them atop the winners’ podium were Lance Recto, Djokovic Garcia, Eilythia Comia and Jasmine Sardona, who also captured singles titles in their respective divisions of the ranking tournament sanctioned by Philta and Universal Tennis and supported by ICON Golf & Sports and Palawan Group of Companies. The fifth-ranked Recto pulled off the biggest upset in the boys’ 12-and-U class, rallying past top seed Harrow Liam, 2-6, 6-1, 6-2, in the finals. His title run also featured victories over No. 2 Raven Licayan, 6-3, 6-7(6), 10-4, in the quarterfinals and third seed Rafael Cablitas, 0-6, 6-1, 6-0, in the semis. Garcia, seeded No. 2, likewise upset top seed Jfsky Berille, 7-5, 3-6, 6-0, to secure the boys’ 14-and-U championship, while top seed Comia dominated Misty May Principe, 6-2, 6-1, for the girls’ 12-and-U title. Sardona claimed the girls’ 18-and-U crown after Elyce Yulpco retired with the score at 1-0. Wong narrowly missed a third title as Palacio and Beatrice Sicangco edged Wong and Danelei Caday, 8-7(7), in a thrilling girls’ 14-and-U doubles final. Palacio, however, still completed a doubles sweep by teaming up with Yulpco to rout Agatha Asistio and Sardona, 8-1, for the girls’ 18-and-U title. In the boys’ doubles, Monte de Ramos and Tulop outlasted Andal and Rombawon, 8-7(2), in the 18-and-U finals, while Garcia and Licayan defeated Drake Garcia and Recto, 8-2, to rule the boys’ 14-and-U division. The Luzon leg resumes with the Mayor Edwin Olivarez Championships on Aug. 6-12 in Sucat, Parañaque before concluding with the Gentry Juniors on Aug. 20-30 at the Colegio de San Agustin Tennis Stadium in San Jose del Monte, Bulacan, culminating with the Gentry Open featuring many of the country’s top-ranked players. For details and registration, contact tournament director Bobby Mangunay at 0915-4046464.

Barbie Forteza shows wild side in ‘Saving Cherry’: 'Iba talaga ito'. It was Barbie Forteza's birthday on July 31. She turned 29. Hard to believe, isn't it? For many of us, Barbie is still the same young girl we've been watching all these years on the small screen. It didn't help that, for years, GMA cast her in roles that highlighted her youthful and innocent image. That's why it comes as such a surprise to see and hear Barbie cursing and shedding that wholesome persona in the recently unveiled trailer of Regal Entertainment's latest film, "Saving Cherry." Without question, it is her boldest and most mature role to date. Barbie herself agrees, admitting that the film pushed her to do things she had never done before. "Oo, parang ganun. Actually, meron kaming isang location na hindi aprub sa magulang ko. Ganung level. Pero excited sila. They're both very excited to see this dahil nga ibang-ibang Barbie ito." It is exactly what she wants. "Alam ko rin naman na pelikula siya, at alam ko rin na gagastos ang manonood nito s o, I made sure na, at least, hopefully, maging worth it yung ibabayad nila. Something na hindi pa nila nakita ever from me." Given her string of successful projects, one might think Barbie would have hesitated before accepting such an audacious role. Apparently, not. "Nag-yes po ako agad. This was pitched to me noong February 2025 sa office ng Regal with everyone actually. Na-overwhelm ako kasi ganun yung treatment at ganun sila kaseryoso to have me on board. Doon pa lang, parang convinced na ako. Kapag ganun yung respeto sa'yo at ganun yung trato sa'yo ng mga katrabaho mo, bakit ka naman hihindi?" Then there's the role itself. "Tapos nalaman ko pa na bagong materyal siya para sa akin. I'm excited for everyone to see it. Sa ilang projects ko, laging sinasabi na ibang Barbie. Pero ito, iba talaga." Barbie even has her own description for Cherry: "The wildest virgin you would ever see." "I play the role of Cherry. She is the wildest woman I have ever portrayed to date. Siya yung wildest and most freeing." She is grateful that she and film director Ivan Payawal shared the same vision. "Binigyan niya kaming lahat ng buong laya as to how we understood every scene. Nakinig siya sa amin. He is really a good captain." It was such that she maintained she was able to "unleash" her "wild side." "Ang saya kasi, aminin naman natin, hindi naman lahat ng mukhang mabait, mabait. Hindi ko rin akalain na meron din akong ganoong side. Wild, pero may dahilan. May lalim." Note the film explores the subject of infidelity. Asked whether cheaters deserve a second chance, Barbie didn't mince words. "F*ck no!" Joining Barbie in "Saving Cherry" are Mikee Quintos, AC Bonifacio, Sassa Gurl, Mika Salamanca, JC Alcantara, Khalil Ramos.

Stronger yen may lift Philippine peso, says MUFG. Japanese financial giant MUFG Bank Ltd. said the Philippine peso is among the Asian currencies that stand to benefit from the Japanese yen’s appreciation against the United States (US) dollar. MUFG Global Markets Research senior currency analyst Michael Wan identified the peso, Thai baht, and Singapore dollar as among the regional currencies that react to the yen’s movements, particularly as market attention has shifted toward the Japanese currency and joint foreign exchange (forex) interventions. “Looking across the Asian forex complex, our analysis shows that the South Korean won, and to a smaller extent the baht, Singapore dollar and peso, in that order, are more sensitive to yen moves,” Wan wrote in an Aug. 4 commentary. “As such, if yen strengthening moves continue, we would expect the won, baht, Singapore dollar, and to a much smaller extent the peso to benefit in the Asia forex context,” Wan added. He noted that in recent weeks, the peso, alongside the baht, Singapore dollar, and won, has maintained a closer relationship with the US dollar-yen exchange rate. Japan and the US are intervening together to prevent Japan from having to sell its holdings of US Treasury bonds to support the yen. This joint cooperation helps maintain market stability by avoiding the need for large asset sales. Meanwhile, Wan said Japan is “unlikely” to sell its US Treasury holdings, given the country’s ample cash reserves of $160 billion, reducing the need for such sales. Additionally, the US has also hinted at expanding the foreign and international monetary authorities (FIMA) facility to provide easier access to short-term dollar liquidity. MUFG’s assessment came as the local currency found support against the greenback on Monday, Aug. 3, closing at ₱60.93 to the US dollar from ₱61.24 last Friday, July 31. Meanwhile, MUFG has revised its near-term exchange rate assumption, expecting the peso to weaken. However, the Japanese lender still expects the local currency to recover gradually and stabilize below the ₱61:$1 level. “Our forecast change largely reflects global factors, and in particular the spikes in oil prices and the resumption in the US-Iran conflict, and as a consequence a slower and perhaps more volatile path towards lower oil prices than previously assumed,” MUFG said. According to the Japanese lender, the US dollar-peso exchange rate is largely influenced by the trade deficit and interbank interest rate differentials, adding that for every 10-percent increase in oil prices, the peso depreciates by nearly one percent. Oil price fluctuations remain among the Philippines’ key external vulnerabilities, given the country’s status as a net oil importer. When the US-Iran war re-escalates, oil supply is disrupted, pushing prices higher. Another threat to the peso is the likelihood of a “super” El Niño, with MUFG citing an 80-percent chance of the weather phenomenon occurring. To support the peso, MUFG has penciled in two more 25-basis-point (bp) increases in the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) key borrowing costs by year-end, allowing the central bank to maintain its hawkish stance. If realized, the key policy rate will reach 5.25 percent from the current 4.75 percent. The Monetary Board (MB) is scheduled to hold its fourth policy meeting of the year on Aug. 27, followed by meetings on Oct. 22 and Dec. 17. This policy tightening, coupled with MUFG’s assumption of “some tentative improvement in government spending,” is expected to support the peso against the greenback.

Japan says combat drones key to adapting to new warfare as tension rises in the region. TOKYO (AP) — Japan needs to adapt to the new methods of warfare like drones and artificial intelligence used in Ukraine and the Middle East and strengthen its defense industry, the government said Tuesday. Japan has bolstered its military capability and spending in recent years and has started deploying long-range cruise missiles as a deterrence to China's military activity. The 598-page defense paper adopted by the Cabinet on Tuesday reiterated that China is Japan’s biggest strategic challenge. Japan is alarmed by the growing presence and frequency of Chinese warships in the Pacific Ocean. Combat drones for new warfare Inspired by the use of drones by Ukraine, Japan considers it is essential to adapt to “new ways of warfare,” the paper said. With many countries racing to develop combat drones, Japan's government prioritizes development of its own for a coastal defense, in combination with long-range missiles. “Speed is key,” Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said in early July. The Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency recently selected four drone makers out of 38 applicants for a rapid development program and that they will advance to testing by Japan's navy in early August before a final selection. A number of companies are developing similar drones. Toshiba announced Friday plans to jointly develop combat drones with startup Pro Drone. Uncrewed weapons could help Japan make up for its decreasing number of service members in a country with a shrinking population. Experts say developing fully homemade drones while Japan’s commercial drone market is dominated by Chinese imports would be a challenge. Alarmed by China’s activity in the Pacific, Russia and North Korea Japan has strengthened its military forces on southwestern islands in recent years and has started deploying long-range cruise missiles, as it worries about a conflict in Taiwan, which China claims as its territory. The paper noted the growing presence Chinese warships and frequency of their activity in the Pacific as a major concern. The Defense Ministry has established a unit dedicated to study Japan’s Pacific strategy and strengthen its defense against China. China has consistently increased its military spending without transparency and strengthened nuclear and missile capability extensively and rapidly, the defense paper said. It noted that in last December Chinese aircraft locked their radars, considered possible preparation for firing missiles, on Japanese planes during Chinese aircraft carrier drills near southwestern Japan. Two Chinese aircraft carriers were spotted last June near the southern Japanese island of Iwo Jima for the first time. This triggered Tokyo's worries about Beijing’s rapidly expanding military activity far beyond its borders and in disputed areas in the East China Sea. Tensions between Tokyo and Beijing have escalated since Takaichi said in November that Chinese military action against Taiwan could justify Japan’s use of force. China’s growing joint military operation with Russia around Japan, including joint bomber flights and warship operations, is also “a grave national security concern,” the paper said. It says North Korea’s rapid development of missiles, including hypersonic arsenals, is an “increasingly serious and pressing threat” and that the North’s growing military ties with Russia and its backing for Moscow's war in Ukraine are a grave concern. Bolstering defense industry, weapons sale Strengthening arms production and technology is essential to Japan's military power, the paper said. The government has been expanding funding for startups and scientific research. In a country that had maintained a pacifist pledge since the end of World War II, many established companies avoid ties to lethal weapons, but a growing number of startups are showing interest in converting dual-use technology for military use, officials say. Japan’s recent scrapping of lethal weapons export ban could also help strengthen the country's underdeveloped defense industry. Weapons technology transfer and joint development and production strengthens both Japanese defense industry base and Japan's ties with its defense partners, said Koizumi, whose travels to other countries have involved arms sales. Japan recently made major deals, including the joint development and transfer of 11 upgraded Mogami-class frigates to Australia. It is discussing a similar deal with New Zealand and has struck a deal to sell retired destroyers to the Philippines.
