Las Piñas schools tighten safety after fatal stabbing. Public schools in Las Piñas have strengthened campus safety measures, urging parents and guardians -- especially those with children in elementary schools -- to provide transparent plastic water bottles or tumblers for their children following the fatal stabbing at Las Piñas National High School. The Schools Division Office (SDO) of Las Piñas said the enhanced measures aim to safeguard the well-being of all learners across the city’s public schools. Officials reminded students not to bring sharp objects to school to prevent accidents and encouraged them to immediately report bullying, harassment, or unusual behavior to teachers, guidance counselors, or administrators for prompt intervention. The reminders were reinforced during an emergency meeting convened by Schools Division Superintendent Melody P. Cruz on Saturday, Aug. 1, with public school principals. Department of Education National Capital Region (DepEd NCR) Regional Director and concurrent Officer in Charge Assistant Secretary for Operations Jocelyn DR Andaya also attended. The meeting, called in the wake of the fatal stabbing, focused on strengthening safety protocols, preventive measures, and closer coordination among schools, parents, local government units, and the community. Andaya stressed the need for collective action to protect learners, saying, “One life taken is a life too many.” She urged school officials, parents, and stakeholders to work together in maintaining safe, secure, and child friendly learning environments. The SDO reiterated its zero-tolerance policy against violence and bullying. Parents, particularly those with elementary school children, were advised to check their children’s bags before school and reinforce positive values, discipline, and responsible behavior at home.

Senate Impeachment Court unites, applauds Alex Eala’s WTA victory. The Senate Impeachment Court, a usually divided body, has united to congratulate tennis star Alex Eala after she victoriously became the first Filipino player to win a Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) 500 singles title. Senate Impeachment Court presiding officer Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero congratulated Eala in behalf of all senator-judges, as well as the prosecution and defense panels. “Even though our views may differ and although both sides are opposing each other in the impeachment court, there are things we should all agree on and unite behind—especially for those who stayed up late last night watching TV,” Escudero said at the start of Day 12 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial. “For me, one of those is the victory and championship of our talented and courageous fellow Filipino, Alex Eala, at the DC Open,” he said. Some senators have also filed separate resolutions commending Eala for winning the 2026 Mubadala DC Open Women’s Singles Championship. Sen. Joel Villanueva, in filing Senate Resolution No. 554, said Eala marked a milestone never before achieved by any Filipino tennis player in the Open Era and firmly establishing her place in Philippine sporting history. “Eala’s historic achievement further enhances the Philippines’ standing in the itnernaitonal sporting community and serves as a lasting testament to the excellence, resilience, discipline and world-class potential of the Filipino athlete, while inspiring future generations to pursue greatness in sports and in service of the nation,” Villanueva said in the resolution. “It is fitting and proper that the Senate of the Philippines recognize and commend Eala whose outstanding achievements have brought honor and distinction to the country and have strengthened national pride through excellence in the field of tennis,” he said. Sen. Paolo “Bam” Aquino IV, in filing Senate Resolution No. 560 also honored Eala for clinching her first WTA Tour-level singles title at the 2026 Mubadala DC Open. “Throughout her championship run, Alex Eala defeated an Olympic gold medalist, a Grand Slam champion, and several of the world’s highest-ranked players, underscoring the extraordinary level of competition she overcame to capture the title,” Aquino said in the resolution. He also emphasized that Eala’s victory underscored the need for the Philippines to increase investments in sports development so more Filipino athletes would be given greater opportunities to excel not only locally but also on the international stage. Sen. Joseph Victor “JV” Ejercito echoed Aquino’s belief saying Eala’s breakthrough highlights the importance of sustained investments in sports development and athlete training. “The succes of Alex Eala shows what Filipino talent can achieve when it is nurtured and supported. Her victory should inspire us to improve our sports development programs, and expand opportunities for young Filipino athletes to train, compete and excel on the world stage,” Ejercito said. Sen. Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan also called for more government support for FIlipino athletes following Eala’s victory. Pangilinan said the government must start bidding to host youth-centered international sports events to give young athletes exposure to elite global sporting standards. “Love may mean nothing to a tennis player. We, her kababayans, draw everything from her matches: anticipation, excitement, patriotic ride and peat (sleepless nights) that’s worth every minute of it,” Pangilinan said.

DSWD: No application needed for UPLIFT assistance, beneficiaries already identified. Eligible beneficiaries of the government's Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) Assistance do not need to apply to receive the cash subsidy, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) said. DSWD Assistant Secretary and spokesperson Irene Dumlao said the UPLIFT program is a targeted social protection measure, with recipients already identified by the government. “Dahil itong UPLIFT assistance ay targeted, ibig sabihin tukoy na po natin kung sino yung makakatanggap ng tulong to cushion the impact of the ongoing energy emergency, hindi na po kinakailangan na mag-apply o magtungo sa isang opisina sapagkat kayo po ay makakatanggap (Since the UPLIFT assistance is targeted, meaning we already know who will receive the aid to cushion the impact of the ongoing energy emergency, there is no need to apply or visit any office because qualified beneficiaries will receive the assistance directly),” Dumlao said. The clarification comes as the government continues distributing financial assistance to vulnerable sectors affected by rising commodity prices amid the energy emergency. DSWD is targeting 7.5 million households under three groups for the UPLIFT Assistance. Group 1 covers 3.5 million beneficiaries of the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) and Walang Gutom Program. They will receive a one-time ₱2,000 assistance. As of Aug. 3, 2.8 million 4Ps households and 214,000 Walang Gutom Program beneficiaries had received the July subsidy, according to the DSWD. Group 2 covers 2.5 million poor and near-poor households identified through the 2024 Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS) who are not beneficiaries of 4Ps or the Walang Gutom Program. They will receive ₱2,000 monthly for six months. A total of 417,000 Group 2 households had received their first payout. Group 3 covers 1.5 million qualified low-wage earners identified through the 2024 CBMS. Eligible beneficiaries will receive ₱2,000 monthly for six consecutive months, from July to December. For employed low-income workers under Group 3, Dumlao said at least 978,000 households had already received the subsidy. Group 3 covers employed workers with a Monthly Salary Credit (MSC) below ₱20,000 who have paid at least one Social Security System (SSS) contribution in 2025 or 2026 and have an active SSS disbursement account. The SSS is responsible for depositing the financial assistance directly into the registered bank or disbursement accounts of qualified beneficiaries. Overall, Dumlao said 4.4 million households had received the ₱2,000 UPLIFT assistance for July across all beneficiary groups. The DSWD said payouts continue nationwide to ensure that all identified beneficiaries receive the assistance intended to cushion the impact of the ongoing energy emergency. Eala’s historic crown comes with hefty payday. More than etching her name in history with her maiden WTA Tour title, Alex Eala walked away from the WTA 500 Mubadala DC Open in Washington, D.C. with a hefty payday. The 21-year-old Filipina tennis sensation earned a whopping $252,000 (around P15.3 million) championship purse after stunning world No. 3 and 2019 champion Jessica Pegula, 4-6, 6-4, 6-0, in the rain-delayed final. The lucrative reward was a fitting bonus for Eala, who battled through a star-studded field and knocked off one elite opponent after another on her way to becoming the first Filipina to win a WTA Tour singles title. Prior to defeating Pegula, she shocked 2024 Paris Olympics champion Zheng Qinwen, defending champion and 2021 US Open finalist Leylah Fernandez, second seed and 2020 Tokyo Olympics bronze winner Elina Svitolina, and third seed and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka. According to her WTA profile, her career prize money has now climbed to $1,537,300 (around P93.6 million). But for the rising Filipina star, the prize purse remains secondary to the milestone she achieved -- a historic WTA crown that will forever stand as her greatest reward.

Senators file resolution honoring Alex Eala’s historic DC Open victory. Senators have filed separate resolutions on Tuesday, Aug. 4, congratulating and commending Filipino tennis star Alexandra Eala for her historic victory at the 2026 Mubadala DC Open, where she became the first Filipino to win a Women's Tennis Association (WTA) Tour-level singles title. Senator Joel Villanueva filed Senate Resolution No. 554, which recognizes Eala's championship run in the WTA 500 tournament in Washington, D.C., calling it a milestone in Philippine sports and a source of national pride. Senators Bam Aquino, Mark Villar and Erwin Tulfo also filed Senate Resolutions 560, 564 and 565, respectively, honoring Eala. In the resolution, Villanueva said Eala's triumph marked "one of the greatest achievements in the history of Philippine sports," noting that her victory firmly established her place in Philippine sporting history. Eala defeated World No. 3 and tournament top seed Jessica Pegula in the championship match to capture the biggest title of her professional career. The resolution also cited that the victory made her the first Filipino to break into the Top 20 of the WTA singles rankings. The measure highlighted Eala's impressive path to the title, which included victories over reigning Olympic women's singles champion Zheng Qinwen, defending DC Open champion Leylah Fernandez, former World No. 3 Elina Svitolina, and four-time Grand Slam champion and former World No. 1 Naomi Osaka, before defeating Pegula in the final. According to the resolution, Eala defeated four Top 10 players during her title run, underscoring the quality of her performance and signaling her emergence among the world's elite women's tennis players. Villanueva also recognized Eala's earlier achievements, including becoming the first Filipino to win a Grand Slam junior singles title at the 2022 US Open, saying she has consistently broken barriers for Philippine tennis and inspired a new generation of Filipino athletes. The senator said Eala's accomplishments have elevated the Philippines' standing in international sports while showcasing the excellence, resilience, discipline, and world-class potential of Filipino athletes. The resolution also praised Eala for exemplifying discipline, perseverance, humility, patriotism, and dedication to excellence, saying these qualities have brought honor, pride, and inspiration to the Filipino people. Aquino emphasized that Eala’s victory underscored the need for the Philippines to increase investments in sports development so that more Filipino athletes are given greater opportunities to excel not just locally, but also on the international stage, and bring honor to the country. “Eala's talent, hard work, discipline, and perseverance, culminating in this remarkable achievement, serve as an inspiration to young Filipinos to pursue their dreams with determination, resilience, and unwavering commitment,” he stressed. Villar said Eala’s remarkable rise is a testament to years of hard work, discipline, and perseverance, adding that her achievements have inspired a new generation of Filipinos to believe that they, too, can compete with the world’s best. “Vamos, Alex! Ang tagumpay mo ay patunay na world-class ang atletang Pilipino. Isa ka nang kampeon, ngunit naniniwala akong marami ka pang maaabot. Pag lumago, hindi na hihinto. Patuloy kang mangarap, magsikap, at ipagmalaki ang Pilipinas sa bawat laban (Your victory is proof that Filipino athletes are truly world-class. You are already a champion, but I believe you still have even greater heights to reach. Once your journey of success begins, there's no stopping you. Keep dreaming, keep working hard, and continue making the Philippines proud in every match. The entire Filipino nation stands behind you, cheering you on every step of the way),” Villar said. Villar also praised Eala’s character, saying her humility and grace have made her an exceptional role model beyond the tennis court. The senator also expressed confidence that Eala’s historic breakthrough is only the beginning of an even brighter career. Meanwhile, Tulfo said that this victory is a defining milestone not only in Philippine tennis but also in the country's sporting history. He added that her achievement serves as a powerful testament to the world-class potential of Filipino athletes and highlights the importance of sustained investment in grassroots sports development, athlete training, and international competition. On the other hand, Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan hailed Filipina tennis sensation Alex Eala’s win, stating that Eala’s win must serve as an inspiration for the Filipino youth and highlighting the positive impact of sports in the lives of many young children.

Plan vs. reality: Commitment lost. Within days of assuming office on July 1, 2022, the Marcos Jr. administration unveiled an ambitious fiscal consolidation plan: the Medium-Term Fiscal Framework 2022–2028 (MTFF 2022–28). This plan was unprecedented in two respects: it was the first framework of its kind in Philippine history and the first to be fully endorsed by both Houses of Congress through a joint resolution. The MTFF 2022–28 became the new administration’s North Star. The MTFF 2022–28 established clear, specific targets. By the end of 2028, the economy was projected to grow by 6.5 percent to 8.0 percent, the public debt-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio was to decline from 61.8 percent to 51.1 percent, and the fiscal deficit was to narrow from 7.6 percent of GDP to 3.0 percent. However, with less than two years left in the current administration’s term, these objectives now appear well beyond reach. Growth has fallen behind plan The economic slowdown has persisted. Growth in 2026 is expected to be weaker than in the preceding year. First-quarter GDP growth came in at a modest 2.8 percent, and the second quarter offers little promise. Socioeconomic Planning Secretary Arsenio Balisacan has projected full-year growth of just 3.5 percent to 4.5 percent—far short of the MTFF target of 6.5 percent to 8.0 percent. Several factors account for this weakness: - Weaker household consumption, driven by high inflation, eroding consumer confidence, slowing economic activity, and rising joblessness, all of which weigh on domestic demand; - Declining foreign direct investment; and - Slowing remittances, strained by challenges in overseas Filipino worker deployment, ongoing conflict in the Middle East, and a sluggish global economy. For the final two years of the Marcos Jr. administration, the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC) revised its GDP growth forecast down to 5.0 percent to 6.0 percent, marking a significant departure from the original MTFF target of 6.5 percent to 8.0 percent. Policymakers lose commitment to fiscal discipline The Covid-19 crisis left a deep mark on the economy, causing a sharp contraction and driving up the national debt-to-GDP ratio. Fiscal consolidation was the appropriate and necessary response. The MTFF 2022–28 set two anchor objectives: reduce the national government debt-to-GDP ratio from 61.8 percent in 2022 to 51.1 percent by 2028, and narrow the fiscal deficit from 7.6 percent of GDP to 3.0 percent over the same period. As of the end of June 2026, the national government’s outstanding debt reached a record high of ₱19.1 trillion (approximately $311.4 billion). It is worth noting that there is no universal threshold at which a debt-to-GDP ratio becomes inherently dangerous. Therefore, a debt-to-GDP ratio around 61.8 percent is not an immediate cause for alarm; in fact, it remains enviable compared to many international peers. For instance, the European Union's Maastricht convergence criteria set a debt-to-GDP ceiling of 60 percent. Global debt-to-GDP averages around 95 percent, while the United States exceeds 120 percent and Japan surpasses 250 percent. Prior to the pandemic, the Philippines maintained a debt-to-GDP ratio of 39.6 percent. Similarly, while the 3.0 percent fiscal deficit target is not sacrosanct, it has long served as a standard benchmark among economists and policymakers. For a developing country like the Philippines—facing an unusually large school-age population and a massive public infrastructure gap—a 3.0 percent deficit-to-GDP ratio represented a balanced and prudent target. Fiscal responsibility requires the government to gradually and credibly reduce its deficit to preserve fiscal buffer space for future economic shocks and keep debt trajectories sustainable. Under the MTFF, the deficit was meant to narrow steadily from 7.6 percent of GDP in 2022 to 3.0 percent in 2028. Instead, after a temporary drop to 7.3 percent in 2022, momentum stalled. In 2024 and 2025, the actual deficit repeatedly breached planned targets, a trend expected to persist through 2028. The implications for debt sustainability are concerning. The primary balance—the fiscal balance net of interest payments expressed as a share of GDP—tells a similar story. The original MTFF targeted a steady improvement from -5.0 percent of GDP in 2022 to -0.8 percent by 2028. Under the revised framework, the projected 2028 primary balance stands at -1.5 percent, pointing to a structurally weaker trajectory. Ultimately, the Executive and Legislative branches appear to have abandoned their commitment to fiscal consolidation. The revised MTFF now plans for a much slower deficit reduction, aiming for 4.8 percent of GDP by 2028 instead of the original 3.0 percent. This 1.8-percentage-point difference is substantial, representing an estimated loss of ₱1.5 trillion in fiscal consolidation between 2026 and 2028. Regrettably, this retreat from fiscal discipline threatens to undermine the country's long-term debt sustainability.

10th Aero Gymnastics Asian tilt unfolds in scenic Tagaytay. Amid the cool, captivating and renewing scenery of Tagaytay City, lively, dynamic and energetic action unfolds starting Wednesday, Aug. 5, with the colorful opening ceremony of the 10th Aero Gymnastics Asian Championships presented by the Philippine Sports Commission at the Tagaytay CT Velodrome. With the theme “Leap, Dance, One Asia,” close to 400 gymnasts from 12 countries are taking part in the three-day meet organized by the Gymnastics Association of the Philippines led by president Cynthia Carrion and sanctioned by the Asian Gymnastics Union. “We are all excited over the staging of this event, which promises to be an entertaining and dynamic festival symbolizing the harmony, unity and camaraderie that sports can achieve among our Asian aerobic gymnasts even in a competitive atmosphere,” Carrion said. “That we are holding the championships in the beautiful city of Tagaytay and at the reconfigured Tagaytay CT Velodrome will be a unique and memorable experience for our participants and fans alike,” she added. Last staged two years ago in Hanoi, Vietnam, the 2026 edition of the continental aero gymnastics showcase will be conducted at the world-class and UCI-certified velodrome, which was modified to accommodate three competition floors plus a 3,000-seat gallery for fans. “We will have a VIP box for our honored guests where they will have a vantage view while the athletes perform and display their artistry and athleticism during the meet,” according to the gymnastics chief. Taking a page from the country’s highly-successful staging 3rd Artistic Gymnastics Junior World Championships last year, organizers have also come up with with a music video “One Asia, One Victory” for the competition also supported by the Philippine Olympic Committee, Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) and Tagaytay City government led by Mayor Brent Tolentino. Carrion disclosed that winners will also get one-of-a-kind medals spotlighting the famed Taal Lake and Volcano, memorable mementoes of their accomplishments from the competition. Cute mascots “Bughaw” and “Lila,” now wearing aerobic tights and leotards, have also been tapped to spice up the tournament and boost sports tourism in the picturesque and progressive city overlooking Taal Lake just a short drive south of Metro Manila. On the other hand, “the 10th Aero Gymnastics Championships is another fine example of using the hosting of international hosting events to boost our top local tourist attractions like Tagaytay City,” noted PSC Chairman Patrick “Pato” Gregorio. “While local tourists are already aware of its reputation as a great tourist destination, there are are still a lot of foreigners who may not know Tagaytay’s natural and man-made charms,” Gregorio, also the head of the National Sports Tourism Interagency Committee, said. He cited the “People’s Park in the Sky,” with its beautiful and panoramic view of Taal Lake and the site of the Shrine of our Lady Mother of Fair Love, which is popular among local tourists, especially during weekends. For those who enjoy bringing their own food and dining outdoors, the Tagaytay Picnic Grove is a family-friendly spot where they can see Taal Lake in all its glory while basking in lush surroundings, according to the PSC honcho. “If our foreign participants feel chilly and want something hot, there is the Mahogany Beef Market nearby where they can have a steaming bowl of bulalo, our Filipino comfort food of beef and bone marrow soup,” he suggested. “Tagaytay City nearly has everything a tourist can offer in a compact and cool location. We are certain that our athletes and officials will be leaving the country with fond memories of the place in spending their time there,” Gregorio said.

PTTF reinforces grassroots program with Intercollegiate, Interscholastic Challenge. The Philippine Table Tennis Federation is set to stage the 2026 Intercollegiate and Interscholastic Challenge from Aug. 28 to 30 at Home Court, Ayala Malls Manila Bay in Parañaque City. Now in its fourth year, the tournament has steadily grown into one of the country's premier competitions for student-athletes, featuring both collegiate and high school divisions as it continues to provide aspiring paddlers with a competitive platform before they move on to the next level. Over the years, the tournament has attracted participation from schools competing in the UAAP, NCAA, UCAL, and CESAFI, as well as the National Academy of Sports, further establishing itself as one of the country's leading grassroots table tennis competitions. PTTF President Ting Ledesma said the tournament's consistent growth has turned it into an event that schools and athletes now look forward to every year. "We're very proud of how the Intercollegiate and Interscholastic Challenge has grown over the past four years," Ledesma said. "What started as an opportunity to bring together the country's best student-athletes has now become an annual tradition on the Philippine table tennis calendar. "We'd also like to extend our heartfelt gratitude to Home Court for its unwavering support through the years. Their partnership has been instrumental in helping us sustain and elevate this tournament for our young athletes." Last year's edition saw the University of Santo Tomas emerge as the most successful school after collecting seven gold medals, highlighted by the collegiate men's singles championship of Eljey Tormis and the high school boys' singles title of Jebb Datahan. For PTTF Secretary-General Pong Ducanes, the tournament serves a much bigger purpose than determining champions. "Our goal has always been to provide student-athletes with a platform where they can showcase their talents," said Ducanes. "We hope this tournament opens doors for them to earn athletic scholarships through table tennis, whether in UAAP, NCAA, UCAL, or CESAFI schools. "Beyond college, we also hope that many of these young players to eventually represent our national team in international competitions." The tournament continues to receive strong backing from longtime partners, with the support of the Huaching Foundation, the Philippine Sports Commission, Home Court Ayala Malls Manila Bay, Topcoms Marketing Inc., Mizuno Philippines, Cara Celine Dormtel, Gold Cross Security Agency, and Best Options Assistance Inc., along with Dino Jalandoni, Bombit Silva, and Eric Ongkauco. Huaching Foundation founder William Yap, whose organization has supported the event over the past several years, emphasized the importance of investing in the next generation of Filipino table tennis players. "The future of Philippine table tennis begins with our youth, and we're happy to continue supporting a tournament that gives them opportunities to compete, improve, and pursue their dreams," Yap said. "We look forward to seeing the tournament continue to grow for many more years."

Woman killed, daughter hurt in Makati shooting; SPD launches manhunt. A 63-year-old woman was killed and her daughter wounded in a gun attack at the corner of Makati Avenue and Durban Street in Barangay Poblacion at 6:46 p.m. on Monday, Aug. 3. The victims were rushed to Makati Medical Center, where the mother was declared dead on arrival and the 26-year-old daughter remains confined with gunshot wounds. Investigators said the assailant, described as wearing a white shirt, maong shorts, and white shoes, fled on foot immediately after the attack. Responding officers led by Col. Pedro A. Alagano Jr. secured the crime scene and launched a dragnet operation with nearby police units. Authorities are conducting an extensive review of closed circuit television (CCTV) footage, including backtracking and forward tracking operations, to trace the suspect’s movements before and after the shooting. The Southern Police District (SPD) has formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to focus on evidence gathering, intelligence operations, case build up, and the manhunt for the gunman. SPD director Brig. Gen. Glenn Oliver C. Cinco assured the victims’ family that all police resources are being mobilized to identify and arrest the suspect. He also appealed to witnesses and anyone with CCTV or dashcam recordings to coordinate with Makati police, stressing that all information will be treated with strict confidentiality.

Adiong raises eyebrows over 'rushed' encashment, spending of OVP confidential funds. Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong believed that the supposed haste by which P125 million was encashed and spent betrayed an alleged effort to misuse the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential funds. Adiong, a spokesperson of the prosecution panel seeking to convict Vice President Sara Duterte in her ongoing Senate impeachment trial, said the speed of the cash transactions must be examined alongside the deficiencies identified in the documents submitted for audit. “Ibig sabihin, kung titingnan natin 'yung pag-encash nito na unusual, na madaliang inencash, madalian talagang ginastos din ito. Dahil madaliang ginastos, hindi tugma-tugma yung dates, at hindi tama 'yung kanilang binigay ng mga documentary evidence to prove that the confidential funds was used in compliance with the Joint Circular ng COA (Commission on Audit),” Adiong said in a press conference Monday, Aug. 3. (That means, if we look at the encashment that was unusual, hurriedly encashed, it was also quickly spent. Because it was quickly spent, the dates do not match, and the documentary evidence they provided is not correct to prove that the confidential funds were used in compliance with the COA Joint Circular.) Former Land Bank of the Philippines (LandBank) officials earlier testified in the hearings that the OVP’s P125-million treasury check was encashed in full after advance coordination with the branch to assemble the unusually large amount of cash. House prosecutor Manila 3rd district Rep. Joel Chua said in the same presser that some acknowledgment receipts (ARs) offered to justify the December 2022 spending indicated dates from a period when the OVP no longer had confidential funds. “Yung ginagamit nilang justification para sa December 2022 ay nasa last quarter ng December 2023. So dito pa lang makikita mo na ang problema,” Chua noted.⠀ (The justification they used for December 2022 is dated in the last quarter of December 2023. So right there you can already see the problem.) “Pangalawa, mayroon pa rin doon na ginamit na justification na ang petsa ay November 2022. Etong buwan na ito wala pang confidential fund dahil ang confidential fund, uulitin ko, ay para sa pechang December 2022,” he added. (Second, there is also a justification dated November 2022. In that month there was still no confidential fund because, I repeat, the confidential fund was for December 2022.) The discrepancies formed part of a wider audit review that began with the OVP’s planning documents and proceeded to the liquidation records and evidence of payment. “Doon sa physical and financial plan ang sabi ng COA hindi siya compliant dahil unang-una hindi specific at hindi particular kung anong confidential activities ang gagawin nila,” Adiong said. (In the physical and financial plan, COA said it was not compliant because, first of all, it was not specific and not particular about what confidential activities they would undertake.) The absence of specific activities prevented auditors from matching the proposed use of the money with the amounts released and the accomplishments later reported by the agency. “So klaro po 'yun, 'iyun po 'yung na-establish natin talaga na meron talagang effort in attempt to really misuse or misappropriate the P125 million confidential funds intended to be used with for the last quarter of 2022,” maintained the Mindanaoan. (So it is clear, that is what we have truly established—that there was indeed an effort and attempt to misuse or misappropriate the P125 million confidential funds intended for use in the last quarter of 2022.)

Payments network elects 2026-2027 board of directors. Stockholders of Payments Network of the Philippines, Inc. elected the 15 members of their Board of Directors for the term 2026-2027 during a special stockholders’ meeting at Makati Shangri-La on Thursday, July 30, 2026. Elected were Reynaldo C. Burgos, representing PNB; Reginaldo Anthony B. Cariaso, representing RCBC; Grace Ofelia Lovely V. Dayo, representing Land Bank; Michael O. De Jesus, representing DBP, Fabian S. Dee, representing Metrobank; Ana Maria A. Delgado, representing Union Bank; Meng Teck Victor Lee, representing Security Bank; Alexander G. Seminiano, representing BPI; Manuel C. Tagaza, representing Chinabank; and Nestor V. Tan, representing BDO. Also elected were independent directors Benjamin P. Castillo, Pedro M. Florescio III, Criselda B. Santillan, Jose Rene D. Villa-Real, and Aristeo P. Zafra, Jr. In the Board’s organizational meeting that followed, the directors unanimously elected Nestor V. Tan as chairman, Fabian S. Dee as president, and Reginaldo Anthony B. Cariaso as treasurer for the term 2026-2027. Payments Network of the Philippines, Inc. is the surviving corporation integrating the operations of BancNet, Inc. and Philippine Clearing House Corporation (PCHC), following the historic approval of their merger by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), the Philippine Competition Commission (PCC), and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) that took effect on June 1, 2026. Payments Network of the Philippines now operates InstaPay and PESOnet, both designated by the BSP as Prominently Important Payment Systems, and Payment vs Payment (PvP) and Philippine Domestic Dollar Transfer System (PDDTS), both BSP- designated as Systematically Important Payment Systems. Other equally significant electronic payment services such as the ATM, Point-of-Sale, check clearing, and direct debit, as well as other electronic payment facilities have also been integrated under one payment network. In the same meeting, the following corporate officers were appointed for the 2026-2027 term: Elmarie S. Reyes, CEO; Emmanuel E. Barcena, COO for PCH Operations; Agnes H. Maranan, Corporate Secretary; Maricelle P. Austria, Head of Human Resources and Administration; Linley V. Julian, Head of Technology and Communications Management for PCH Operations; Jennie F. Lansang, Chief information Officer; Arnel G. Lim, Chief Audit Executive; Myra S. Privado, Head of Software Testing and Certification; Mabelyn Tagasa, Deputy Chief Information Officer; Roel Dennis S. Tan, Chief Risk and Compliance Officer; Roseanne T. Tan, Head of Business and Relationship Management; and Jonalyn V. Villasin, Head of Finance and Accounting.

Maynilad H1 profit climbs 14% on lower financing costs. West Zone concessionaire Maynilad Water Services Inc. reported a 14-percent increase in net income in the first half, driven by lower interest expense and taxes, which more than offset higher operating expenses (opex). In a media briefing on Tuesday, Aug. 4, Maynilad President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Ramoncito S. Fernandez said the company’s improved operational performance boosted first-half net income to ₱8.51 billion from ₱7.47 billion in the same period last year. “We improved water surface coverage, reduced water losses, expanded wastewater and sanitation coverage, and sustained investments in infrastructure and network. These operational gains supported our financial performance and strengthened our ability to continue investing in the West,” Fernandez said. Meanwhile, consolidated revenues rose four percent to ₱19.11 billion, while earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) increased 7.5 percent to ₱13.7 billion. Furthermore, the company’s billed connections increased 1.6 percent to 1.58 million, while total billed volume rose to 280.8 million cubic meters during the period. Maynilad’s non-revenue water (NRW), or water produced but lost or unbilled before reaching customers, declined to 29.7 percent in the January-to-June period. To date, the company has spent about ₱12.89 billion in capital expenditures (capex) during the first half of the year, funding water and wastewater infrastructure, network efficiency and reliability, facilities, and other customer service improvements. Ricardo Delos Reyes, Maynilad’s chief financial officer (CFO), said the company may reduce its full-year capital spending to ₱28 billion from the initial ₱30-billion plan. According to the CFO, Maynilad is also weighing the option of tapping the equity market. “By the end of the year, it depends on our capex spending for this year. At the moment, we are on track to deliver our budget, but if it falls short of that, then probably we won’t need it anymore,” he told reporters. “We might advance our borrowings for next year, but it all depends on the interest rates.” As preparations continue for the possible return of El Niño, state-run Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) recently allocated 46 cubic meters per second (CMS) of water from Angat Dam. Christopher Lichauco, Maynilad’s chief operating officer (COO), confirmed that the company has begun discussions to secure a higher allocation. Lichauco said the ideal allocation for Maynilad would be more than 60 percent. “We have a reinforcement, we have La Mesa Dam, aside from Angat. We placed [water pumps] for added reinforcement to be able to draw water from La Mesa,” he added, noting that the reservoir is shared with East Zone concessionaire Manila Water Co. Inc.

Another world, 30 years on. Most resorts sell rooms. Plantation Bay, A Real Resort With A Real Spa has always sold something far more elusive: the feeling of stepping into another world. That, according to founder J. Manuel “Manny” Gonzalez, was the vision from the very beginning. Long before “experiences” became hospitality’s favorite buzzword, he set out to create a place where guests could retreat from the pace of everyday life. “We were never selling rooms,” he simply says. “We were selling an experience.” Celebrating its 30th anniversary this year, Plantation Bay remains unmistakably shaped by its founder. Every corner bears the imprint of Manny’s curiosity, exacting standards, and wide-ranging passions: food, art, travel, history, and more. Nearly everything here has a story. The “real resort with a real spa” feels almost like an autobiography written in its lagoons, landscaping, restaurants, paintings, and countless thoughtful details. Over three decades, it has evolved chapter by chapter, each addition reflecting the interests and convictions of the man behind it. The milestone unfolded at Galapagos Beach, where guests, dressed in shades of white, ivory, pearl, and champagne, gathered to celebrate. The evening featured a gourmet menu, a retrospective on the resort’s journey, performances by the staff, and a fireworks display over the water. More telling than the festivities during the July 16 anniversary event, however, was the guest list. It reflected the team’s priorities: former general managers, longtime shareholders, artists, collaborators, travel partners, and friends who have become part of the resort's story through the years. Among those present were artist Romulo Galicano, whose works have long formed part of the resort’s visual identity; former Cebu governor Gwendolyn Garcia, actors Paul Jake Castillo and Kaye Abad, alongside members of the Plantation Bay family who have helped shaped its legacy. In an age when destinations compete to offer the new next attraction, Plantation Bay’s greatest strength may simply be its unwavering sense of place. No man is an island, as the saying goes. Yet for the past 30 years, Manny Gonzalez has come remarkably close, creating a world of his own and inviting generations to make it part of their own stories.

‎Flood, power cuts batter La Union. SAN FERNANDO CITY, La Union -- Hundreds of residents were displaced while several areas in La Union were affected by flooding, power interruptions, and a landslide from heavy rains caused by tropical cyclone Luis and the southwest monsoon. ‎ ‎The La Union Provincial Information Office said 27 weather-related incidents were monitored in the province as of 9 a.m. on Tuesday, Aug. 4. ‎ ‎Knee-deep flooding was reported in the municipalities of Bauang, Santo Tomas, and Naguilian, as well as the City of San Fernando. ‎ ‎A landslide and fallen trees were also reported in Naguilian, while power interruptions affected 34 barangays in Bauang, Naguilian, and San Fernando. ‎ ‎A total of 159 families, or 484 individuals, are staying in evacuation centers in Naguilian and Bagulin. ‎ ‎Another 29 families, or 99 individuals, are temporarily sheltered outside evacuation centers. ‎ ‎Meanwhile, 61 families in the municipalities of Bauang and Aringay were preemptively evacuated as a precaution against possible flooding and landslides. ‎ ‎Provincial officials urged residents in vulnerable areas to remain alert and follow the directives of local disaster management officials. ‎ ‎ The provincial government suspended classes and work in government offices on Tuesday, Aug. 4, following the issuance of an Orange Rainfall Warning due to inclement weather. ‎ ‎The suspension under Executive Order No. 41 seeks to ensure public safety as heavy rains continue to affect the province. ‎ ‎Suspension of work in private companies was encouraged. ‎ ‎Offices delivering essential services, including health, disaster risk reduction and management, and emergency response, will remain fully operational. ‎ ‎Residents were advised to stay indoors and take necessary precautions against flooding and rain-related hazards. ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎

How to setup Apple Pay. With anticipation and hype, Apple Pay is officially available in the Philippines, providing contactless and card-less payments for iPhone and Apple Watch users. The rollout begins through Apple’s Wallet app, where partnered cards can be registered within moments. Users don’t have to input card details; all they have to do is tap their credit or debit cards onto their iPhones. Then users can begin their shopping spree with Apple Pay. Users do not need to be online for this, meaning your iPhone or Apple Watch doesn’t need to be connected to the Wi-Fi or have their data enabled. How to setup Open the Wallet app in your iPhone. Tap the + sign above. You will have an option “Debit or Credit Card.” Tap that. You will get a quick information page and “Continue” button to tap. After that you get instructions telling you to tap your iPhone at the back of the card. Then you’re all set. You can set multiple cards to one Apple Pay account. The first card you’ve registered will be the default card. The more cards you register, they are arranged into a stack, which you can flip through to choose which one you want to use for a purchase. Users can also pay using the Apple Watch. Users only have to open their Wallet app through the Watch, double press the side button to activate, then scan on the POS device. So far, partnered banks include GoTyme, Union Bank, Metrobank, and Chinabank. More are expected to roll out in the coming months. Users also have the option to use Apple Pay over at Shopee, whether browser or mobile app.

'Sarap ng pakiramdam': Speaker Dy hails Eala for capturing DC Open crown. Like the rest of Filipinos, House Speaker Faustino “Bojie” Dy III is in cloud nine following Alex Eala's 2026 Mubadala DC Open victory, her first ever Women's Tennis Association (WTA) Tour title, on early Tuesday morning, Aug. 4. In a social media post, Dy lauded Eala for becoming the first Filipino to win a WTA Tour singles title. He called the achievement a milestone not only for Philippine tennis but for the entire nation. “Ang sarap ng pakiramdam na makita kang manalo (It feels so good to see you win, Alex),” said the Speaker from Isabela's 6th district. Dy said the 21-year-old tennis sensation's historic victory was the product of years of hard work and sacrifice that have inspired pride and joy among millions of Filipinos. "Nakakatuwang isipin na ang pinaghirapan ng isang Pilipina ay nakapagpasaya sa milyun-milyong Pilipino.” (It is heartening to think that what a Filipina worked hard for brought joy to millions of Filipinos.) The Speaker said Eala’s success reflects the rewards of perseverance, discipline, and commitment to excellence, noting that her journey continues to inspire young Filipinos to pursue their dreams regardless of the challenges they face. “Congratulations on your first WTA title. You make every Filipino proud every time you step on the court. Maraming salamat (Thank you very much),” he said. Eala completed a remarkable championship run at the Mubadala Citi DC Open in Washington, where she defeated reigning Olympic champion Qinwen Zheng, defending champion Leylah Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina, and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka on the way to the finals. In the championship, Eala rallied past World No. 3 and top seed Jessica Pegula, 4-6, 6-4, 6-0, in the final to capture her maiden WTA Tour singles title. The victory is expected to lift the Eala to a career-high World No. 20 in the WTA rankings.

‎Basilan town listed as high-risk area in BARMM polls. ZAMBOANGA CITY - The Commission on Elections has included the town of Al-Barka in Basilan province in the red list category, a list of high-risk areas in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao elections in September. ‎ ‎High-risk areas are places exhibiting the highest risk level due to a combination of active armed insurgent groups, intense local political rivalries, and a history of election-related violence. ‎ ‎Al-Barka has 13,664 voters. ‎ ‎Two municipalities in the province were included by the Comelec in the orange category, towns flagged due to serious security threats posed by lawless elements. ‎ ‎These are Tipo Tipo with 14,960 voters and Tabuan-Lasa with 18,140 voters. ‎ ‎The list was prepared in connection with the elections on Sept. 14. ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎

Visa brings Apple Pay to its customers in the Philippines. Visa (NYSE: V), a global leader in digital payments, announced today, Aug. 4, that Visa debit and credit cardholders in the Philippines can now add their eligible cards to Apple Pay on their iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad, and Mac. Apple Pay is an easy, secure and private way to pay in-store, in-app and online. This announcement accelerates the digitalization of payments all while expanding payment options for Filipinos traveling abroad and visitors traveling to the Philippines. Across the Asia Pacific region, 97% of travelers say that they will bring credit, debit, or prepaid cards on their trips, while only 17% intend to bring foreign currency. Among travelers, 38% said they prefer cards because of robust security and fraud protection features, while 20% cite wide acceptance. Apple Pay seamlessly delivers on these exact needs by making everyday transactions easy, secure, and private. To pay in-store, customers simply double-click the side button, authenticate, and hold their iPhone or Apple Watch near a payment terminal to make a contactless payment. Every Apple Pay purchase is secure because it is authenticated with Face ID, Touch ID, or device passcode, as well as a one-time unique dynamic security code. Apple Pay is accepted in grocery stores, pharmacies, restaurants, coffee shops, retail stores, and many more places that accept contactless payments. Customers can also use Apple Pay on iPhone, iPad, and Mac to make faster and more convenient purchases in apps or on the web without having to create accounts or repeatedly type in contact information, card details, or shipping and billing information. “Apple Pay represents the next evolution of payments in the Philippines, combining ease of use, simplicity, and security in every transaction, helping amplify the payment experience for Visa cardholders in the Philippines. With Apple Pay, Filipinos and tourists alike now have seamless and secure ways to pay across shops, restaurants, travel destinations, and public transport, supporting the nation’s vision to become a cash-lite economy,” said Jeffrey Navarro, Country Manager for Visa Philippines. Security and privacy are at the core of Apple Pay. When customers use a credit or debit card with Apple Pay, the actual card numbers are not stored on the device, nor on Apple servers. Instead, a unique Device Account Number is assigned, encrypted and securely stored in the Secure Element, an industry-standard, certified chip designed to store the payment information safely on the device. Apple Pay is easy to set up. On iPhone, simply open the Wallet app, tap the ‘+’, and follow the steps to add a Visa card. Once a customer adds a card to iPhone, Apple Watch, iPad, and Mac, they can start using Apple Pay on that device right away. Customers will continue to receive all of the rewards and benefits offered by their Visa cards. For more information on Apple Pay, visit: https://www.apple.com/ph/apple-pay/

Comply with human rights, proper procedure in police operations, cops told. The Philippine National Police (PNP) ordered all police commanders to strengthen compliance with human rights in all police operations as the country observes the 77th International Humanitarian Law Month this August. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr. said the directive was intended to ensure that every police operation remains anchored on the rule of law while safeguarding the rights and dignity of civilians, particularly in conflict-affected areas. He said this is part of the ongoing measures to maintain the integrity, discipline and professionalism of the police force. “Our personnel will continue to undergo regular training, closely coordinate with partner agencies, and strictly follow operational procedures that prioritize the protection of civilians while effectively addressing security threats,” said Nartatez. August is observed as International Humanitarian Law Month to raise awareness of the legal protections afforded to civilians and other noncombatants during armed conflict International Humanitarian Law governs the conduct of armed conflict and protects civilians, the wounded, medical personnel, and others who are no longer taking part in hostilities. Nartatez said the PNP continues to draw lessons from the 2017 Marawi siege, where law enforcement and security forces faced complex operational challenges while carrying out missions against terrorist groups. He noted that the conviction of members of the Maute group showed that justice is achieved through lawful and accountable institutions. “I remind every police officer that professionalism is measured not only by mission accomplishment but also by respect for human dignity. Even in the most challenging security operations, exercise restraint, protect civilians, and uphold the law at all times,” said Nartatez.

Festival Main Mall drives FILRT’s 34% H1 profit growth. Filinvest REIT Corp. (FILRT), the real estate investment trust (REIT) of the Gotianun Group, reported a 34-percent increase in net income to ₱874 million in the first half of 2026, allowing it to declare a ₱391-million cash dividend for the second quarter. In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, Aug. 4, the firm said it generated ₱2.05 billion in revenue in the first half, up 31 percent year-on-year, driven mainly by the full-period contribution of the recently acquired Festival Main Mall. Costs and expenses were prudently managed at ₱663 million, up eight percent, while other charges declined one percent to ₱185 million. FILRT’s portfolio comprises 17 office buildings, one mall, and one resort lot, with a total gross leasable area (GLA) of 452,310 square meters (sqm). Average occupancy reached 87 percent in the first half, steady from the previous quarter and six percentage points (ppts) higher than a year ago. The addition of Festival Main Mall in May last year lifted portfolio occupancy and helped offset softer office rental rates. The portfolio’s tenant mix consists of 61-percent office, 32-percent retail, and seven-percent hospitality properties. In the office segment, which recorded an average occupancy of 80 percent in the first six months of 2026, multinational business process outsourcing (BPO) companies accounted for 85 percent of occupied space, traditional tenants for 13 percent, and the remainder for coworking, wellness, and educational institutions. As of June 2026, FILRT had secured 5,964 sqm of new leases from incoming tenants and existing occupants expanding within Northgate Cyberzone. On tenant retention, 49 percent of the 20,689 sqm of leases expiring this year had been renewed or were covered by signed renewal letters of intent. As of end-June, the portfolio’s weighted average lease expiry (WALE) stood at 13.95 years. “Our first-half performance reflects the resilience of our portfolio. As we move through the rest of 2026, we will remain focused on disciplined leasing, prudent cost management, and sustainability-led initiatives that support stable dividends and long-term shareholder value,” said FILRT President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Maricel Brion-Lirio. FILRT said its board of directors approved regular quarterly cash dividends of ₱0.06 per outstanding common share for shareholders of record as of Aug. 20, 2026, payable on Sept. 1, 2026. This brings FILRT’s total declared dividends for 2026 to ₱0.18 per common share, or a total of ₱1.17 billion, equivalent to an annualized yield of 8.2 percent based on its closing share price of ₱2.92 on Aug. 3, 2026. The latest quarterly dividend covers the April-to-June 2026 income period. - James A. Loyola

Fresh off WTA title, Eala faces bigger test in Toronto. There will be little time for Alex Eala to savor her breakthrough WTA Tour title as she is expected to quickly shift her focus to an even tougher test at the National Bank Open in Toronto, Canada this week. The WTA 1000 event has been underway since last Sunday, Aug. 2, with Eala securing an opening-round bye and the 25th seeding. Tournament organizers initially scheduled Eala’s opening round match for Wednesday night, Aug. 5 (Thursday night, Aug. 6, Philippine), where she was set to face American Alycia Parks, who defeated qualifier Victoria Jimenez Kasintseva, 6-4, 6-4. It will be the second meeting between Eala and Parks, with the American winning their first and only matchup in the first round of the Australian Open last January, 0-6, 6-3, 6-2. But much has changed since then, with both players having made significant strides in the rankings. Eala surged from No. 49 at the time to career-high No. 20 this week, while Parks has also improved, climbing from No. 99 to No. 71. More than meeting Parks, Eala is also expected to be cautious of what lies ahead deeper in the bracket, where she is in the lower half of the draw that has reigning Wimbledon champion and sixth seed Linda Noskova, No. 21 Marie Bouzkova, No. 12 Belinda Bencic, qualifier Sloane Stephens, and good friend No. 13 Iva Jovic, to name a few. After the National Bank Open, Eala is also scheduled for the Cincinnati Open -- another WTA 1000 event -- set Aug. 13 to 23 which serves as a buildup for the US Open slated Aug. 30 to Sept. 13.

Economic, labor experts to be invited in LTFRB fare hike hearing. Economic and labor experts will be invited in the next hearing for the fare increase petitions of public utility vehicles (PUVs), the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) said. LTFRB chairman Vigor D. Mendoza II said those experts are expected to shed light on the effects of fare increase of any amount amid the ongoing hearing in the petition of at least seven transport groups for fare hike. Among the government agencies that will be invited are the Department of Economy, Planning and Development (DEPDev), the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE), and the Department of Energy (DOE). “We all heard the concerns and arguments raised by the transport groups on their fare hike petitions. They are all valid and legitimate and our task now is to validate the data they presented in terms of operational costs vis-à-vis their daily income and that of the drivers,” said Mendoza. “But we also need to hear what the DEPDev and other agencies concerned have to say because we are all aware that any fare adjustment of any amount will have effects on the economy and the public’s purchasing power,” he added. On Monday, representatives from transport and commuter groups attended the hearing for fare hike petition that were filed amid the series of oil price hikes. With the arguments and concerns of those invited on Monday hearing, Mendoza said the next step is to hear what economic experts would say. For the DEPDEv, Mendoza said they want to hear the effects of any amount that will be proposed based on the petitions of the transport groups while DOLE is expected to discuss what should be accorded and due to the workers, in this case, the drivers of public utility vehicles (PUVs). The DOE, for its part, will discuss matters pertaining to the oil price hikes and its effects on motorists. Mendoza explained that they need to factor in the wisdom and expertise of the concerned agencies in the goal of coming up with the best solution that is acceptable to the PUV sector and the commuting public. “The necessity to assist the PUV sector is already there because of the series of oil price hikes in the past weeks. The question, however, is that if fare adjustments are approved, what would be the ideal amount that would have the most minimal inflationary effects but are acceptable to everybody,” said Mendoza. “This is the part where the insights of experts from DEPDev and other concerned agencies will play a key role,” he added.

DOE eyes cheaper power bills with off-grid RE auction. The Department of Energy (DOE) is planning a dedicated renewable energy (RE) auction for off-grid islands in a bid to lower consumers’ electricity bills by reducing the universal charge for missionary electrification (UCME). Energy Undersecretary Rowena Guevara said during a recent media briefing that the DOE is preparing a new round of the Green Energy Auction (GEA) specifically for off-grid areas served by state-run National Power Corp. (Napocor). The GEA for Napocor is designed to replace costly diesel-fired power plants with RE facilities and battery energy storage systems (BESS), improving energy security while reducing the cost of missionary electrification, which is recovered from consumers nationwide through UCME. According to Guevara, the initiative is expected to ease the financial burden on consumers, noting that the average true cost of power generation in off-grid areas is about ₱18 per kilowatt-hour (kWh), while generation costs in some remote islands can reach as high as ₱62/kWh. Replacing diesel-fired generation in these areas is expected to significantly lower electricity costs. “We are targeting 20 islands, specifically the larger ones, to be auctioned off [to RE developers]. We had a focus group discussion (FGD) last week for the potential developers and the local government unit (LGU) of select islands,” she said. “Right now, because the prices for solar plus battery systems keep going down, we want to replace the diesel plants in the Napocor area with those.” The DOE is finalizing the auction parameters and the list of the 20 target islands, with the auction expected to be launched next year. The actual reduction in UCME will depend on the winning bids submitted by developers during the auction. “At the end of the day, when the GEA for Napocor becomes successful, we can lower the cost of UCME,” Guevara said.

Caloocan jeepney drivers to get P10K under free ride program. Caloocan jeepney drivers will get up to P10,000 each from the city’s free ride program, which guarantees income while commuters enjoy no fare trips amid rising fuel costs. City officials said each participating driver will earn P2,500 for four hours of trips per day. The program will run for four days, allowing drivers to collect a total of P10,000. The initiative will be carried out in coordination with 2,700 members of Jeepney Operators and Drivers Associations (JODA). Commuters can ride for free on designated jeepney routes, while drivers are assured of guaranteed income from the city government. Officials added that the program aims to ease the burden of higher fuel costs on both commuters and drivers. Interested drivers were advised to coordinate with their respective JODA presidents. Routes covered by the free ride program will be announced separately. The city government said the initiative is part of its broader effort to support communities affected by the global fuel crisis.

2 wounded in Makati shooting over drug dispute. Two men allegedly linked to a series of robberies and hold-up incidents were shot and wounded by two other suspects during an alleged dispute over illegal drug proceeds in Makati City on Saturday, Aug. 1. Police said the incident happened around 1 a.m. on Hiwaga Street in Barangay Olympia. Investigators believe the clash stemmed from a quarrel over the division of illegal drug profits. The victims, identified only as “Christian,” 26, and “Khen,” 23, each sustained gunshot wounds to the right arm. Both are in stable condition at Makati Medical Center. Authorities said the suspects, “Rudy,” 34, and “Teejay,” 31, were also linked to robbery and hold-up cases across Metro Manila. Recovered at the scene were a black Yamaha Aerox motorcycle, a SWAT marked tactical vest, spray paint cans, and bloodied clothing. A 9mm pistol and a .45-caliber pistol were later found along the suspects’ escape route. Police also seized a blue black Honda Click motorcycle believed to be the getaway vehicle, along with clothing and other items tied to the crime. Makati police chief Col. Pedro Alagano Jr. led the pursuit that tracked the suspects to Tramo Street, Barangay 64, Pasay City. Southern Police District director Brig. Gen. Glenn Oliver Cinco said intelligence operations are underway to locate and arrest the suspects.

PNP commanders tasked to expand community-based intel network vs illegal gambling. Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr., chief of the Philippine National Police (PNP), ordered all police commanders down to the precinct and station levels to intensify community intelligence efforts to dismantle illegal gambling operations and hubs across the country. Aside from popular card and street gambling, police are also intensifying operations against online platforms of illegal gambling. “Illegal gambling breeds other crimes—from domestic violence to theft, robbery and even crimes against persons. And this is the reason why your PNP has been very aggressive in its campaign as manifested by our monthly accomplishment reports,” said Nartatez. He explained that information from residents remains one of the most effective tools in identifying illegal gambling operations that continue to operate in different parts of the country. Police have sustained its anti-illegal gambling campaign through intensified police operations nationwide. For July this year, a total of 9,401 persons were arrested while more than P3.2 million worth of bet money and gambling paraphernalia were confiscated. Nartatez said the campaign is not limited to Metro Manila as he said police resources are also being mobilized in municipalities, provinces, and far-flung communities where illegal gambling operations continue to thrive. “Our operations are not only focused in Metro Manila. The same level of aggressive operations has been ongoing in municipalities and provinces, including far-flung areas,” he said. He said illegal gambling is not merely a law enforcement concern because it also contributes to the commission of other crimes as revealed in the PNP crime data. Nartatez said dismantling illegal gambling operations will also help improve peace and order in communities.

6-year-old Maldia finishes second in Bangkok chess tilt. Anthony Maldia showed some promise after placing second in the rapid Under-7 division of the 2nd Bangkok Summer International Chess Open in Bangkok, Thailand held recently. The six-year-old woodpusher posted 5.5 points out of the possible seven in his maiden international tournament, finishing just half a point behind eventual winner Ian Jung of South Korea. Thailand’s Nutpisit Suthiponpaisarn came in third with 5 points. Maldia started the tournament with a draw with China’s Sha Qihao, before racking up victories over fellow Filipina Sophie Hillary Estavillo, Thailand’s Teerata Kasempsup and Korea’s Kim Kangbin. He absorbed his lone defeat against Jung, but bounced back with back-to-back wins over Thais Suthiponpaisarn and Pryn Wantanakorn Vessawan to finish the tournament on a high note. Over 7,700 families hit, nearly 4,000 individuals displaced due to ‘Luis,’ ‘habagat’ – OCD. More than 7,700 families have been affected while nearly 4,000 people have been displaced by the combined effects of the enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) and the remnants of Tropical Depression Luis, according to initial data released Tuesday, Aug. 4, by the Office of Civil Defense (OCD). OCD spokesperson Junie Castillo said 7,700 families from 17 barangays have been affected by the weather disturbance. Of those, about 1,200 families, or nearly 4,000 individuals, have sought shelter in evacuation centers. “The initial data are not limited to Northern Luzon. They also include affected communities in the Bicol Region and Mindanao because these figures cover the effects of the southwest monsoon,” Castillo said. Luis developed on Aug. 1 before making landfall over Maconacon, Isabela on Aug. 3, and eventually weakened into a low pressure area (LPA) later that day. Although Luis has dissipated, Castillo said habagat continues to bring heavy rains over several parts of the country. Castillo said authorities have so far recorded 17 flooded areas in Ilocos (Region 1), Zamboanga Peninsula (Region 9), and the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). Despite Luis weakening into an LPA, the OCD has maintained the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Operations Center (NDRRMOC) under “Blue Alert” status. “This means we are under heightened monitoring and different government agencies remain on standby,” Castillo said. "This is not only at the national operations center. Even the regional disaster operations centers remain on Blue Alert status. In fact, in Region 1, different response clusters are already on standby in case our fellow Filipinos need assistance,” he added. Castillo said Pangasinan remains under close watch because the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) continues to forecast intense rainfall. “We are monitoring our fellow Filipinos, especially in Pangasinan, because the expected heavy rainfall will occur there due to the red rainfall warning being in effect. Residents in low-lying areas, flood-prone communities and places vulnerable to landslides should be evacuated if necessary,” he said. Orange rainfall warnings also remain in effect over La Union, Benguet, Tarlac, Zambales and Bataan. The OCD also cited the Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB), which identified about 5,000 barangays nationwide as vulnerable to landslides and flooding. These include 32 barangays in Cagayan Valley (Region 2), 345 in the Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) ,and 21 in Mimaropa (Region 4B) under the 100-millimeter rainfall threshold. No confirmed deaths or missing persons have been reported as of Tuesday, Castillo said. However, the OCD said it was verifying reports that a 21-year-old young man allegedly drowned in Lingayen, Pangasinan after attempting to bathe in a deep excavation. “Our message to our fellow Filipinos is to listen to the advice of local authorities. Know exactly what you need to do. If you are told to evacuate, stay alert and know what is happening. While it is still daylight and you can see the conditions, prepare. Do not wait until nighttime,” Castillo said. He added that food and non-food relief items had already been prepositioned in vulnerable areas to support affected families if conditions worsen.

Petron’s profits fall 27% even as fuel revenues soared past ₱600 billion. Petron Corp., the country’s sole remaining oil refiner, reported a 27 percent drop in its first-half net income as Middle East geopolitical volatility and temporary refinery shutdowns weighed on its financial performance. In a statement on Tuesday, Aug. 4, Petron said net income for the first six months of 2026 slipped to ₱3.8 billion from the same period last year. Earnings were heavily impacted by record-high crude prices, elevated import premiums, and soaring freight expenses. External pressures were driven by ongoing conflict involving the United States (US) and Iran, which fueled extreme volatility across global oil markets. Benchmark Dubai crude peaked at $129 per barrel in March before easing to $79 per barrel in June, according to the oil firm. Overall, Dubai crude averaged $91 per barrel for the first half of the year—a 27 percent surge compared to 2025. Operational challenges further restricted refining capacity. Output was curtailed by a temporary shutdown at the Port Dickson Refinery in Malaysia and a scheduled first-quarter maintenance turnaround at the company’s Bataan facility in Limay. To ensure product availability, Petron initiated limited refining operations in Malaysia using existing crude inventory while construction continues on a replacement jetty, set for commissioning in early 2027. Despite these disruptions, consolidated sales volume rose six percent to 67.9 million barrels. An 86 percent surge in trading transactions by the company’s Singapore subsidiary offset a six percent decline in combined domestic and Malaysian sales, which totaled 52.9 million barrels. In the domestic retail fuel segment, the company posted a strong 15 percent growth. Driven by higher prices and volume gains, consolidated revenues jumped 57 percent to ₱605.9 billion. However, elevated operating costs and expensive feedstock squeezed margins, pulling operating income down 17 percent to ₱12.6 billion. Petron Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Ramon S. Ang assured stakeholders that despite first-half challenges driven by market volatility, the company remains focused on meeting national fuel demand. “While the first half of the year has been challenging, we are confident that our financial discipline, operational resilience, and competitive strengths will enable us to navigate these temporary headwinds,” Ang said. To enhance supply reliability, Petron is advancing several key infrastructure developments. Its 180,000-metric-ton annual capacity coco-methyl ester (CME) plant at the Bataan Refinery is nearing completion to secure internal biofuel supplies. Additionally, the company is expanding terminal capacity, including four new storage tanks in Limay scheduled for completion by early 2028, along with an LPG mounded tank and canister filling unit in Bacolod targeted for late 2028. (Gabriell Christel Galang)

Luxury condo sales lift Shang Properties’ first-half profit. Based on the firm’s financial statement (FS) filed with the Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) on Tuesday, Aug. 4, the increase in earnings was also supported by continued growth in its condominium, rental and cinema, and hotel operations. Revenues rose 11.3 percent to ₱5.9 billion in the first half of the year from ₱5.3 billion in the same period of 2025. Meanwhile, revenue from hotel operations rose two percent to ₱2.38 billion, supported by a higher occupancy rate at Shangri-La The Fort, Manila during the second quarter of 2026 compared with the same period last year. Income from operations before interest, share in joint venture (JV) income, and income tax increased 9.2 percent to ₱1.98 billion from ₱1.81 billion in the first half of 2025, reflecting revenue growth and effective cost management. - James A. Loyola

Palace: Transport strike not the solution to issues. Malacañang has urged transport groups to engage in dialogue and negotiate with the government rather than take their concerns to the streets, stressing that a transport strike is not the solution to the issues at hand. Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said while they do not prevent the groups' right to protest, she advised them to negotiate with the government, noting that President Marcos is open for dialogues. "Muli, ang nais ng gobyerno, ang nais ng pamahalaan ay pag-uusap, negosasyon, makita kung ano ang daing at kung mayroon man magkakaroon ng transport rally, hindi po kasi ito ang tugon, hindi ito ang sagot sa mga ganitong klaseng issue dahil mas mahihirapan lang din po ang ating mga commuters sa gagawin ganitong klaseng aksyon (Once again, what the government wants is dialogue and negotiation, to hear the concerns being raised. If there will be a transport rally, we do not believe that it is the appropriate response or solution to these kinds of issues because it will only make things more difficult for our commuters)," Castro said in a Palace briefing on Tuesday, Aug. 4. "Kayo naman po ay nadidinig ng gobyerno, mas maganda na magkaroon ng matahimik, maayos na diyalogo, hindi yung lagi tayo nasa daan dahil hindi po siya ang sagot sa ating mga isyu sa ngayon (The government is listening to you. It would be better to have a peaceful and orderly dialogue rather than taking to the streets all the time, because that is not the answer to the issues we are facing at the moment)," Castro added. "But, hindi po natin pinipigilan ang sinumang nais na magkaroon ng pagpoprotesta, but still hindi po siya makakatulong sa ating ekonomiya (We are not preventing anyone from exercising their right to protest. However, such actions will not help our economy)," the Palace official further said. Manibela and other transport groups will stage a three-day transport strike from Aug. 10 to 12 to call on the government to grant a provisional fare hike amid high fuel prices. Castro directly addressed Manibela, saying that whatever they want to raise, the government is ready to respond. "Manibela, kung anuman po ang nais ng Manibela, handa naman po tumugon ang ating pamahalaan para hindi naman mahirapan ng ating mga commuters sa araw na ito ay kanilang gagawin (Manibela, Whatever Manibela wants to raise, the government is ready to respond so that our commuters will not be inconvenienced on the day of the strike)," Castro said. On the fresh fare hike petition filed by several transport groups, the Palace spokesperson said the President hopes that the decision on the petition will not adversely affect the commuters. "Ang sabi naman ng Pangulo, sana ay hindi makaapekto kung magkakaroon man ng pagtaas ng pamasahe o hindi magkakaroon ng taas ng pamasahe, ayaw po sanang makaapekto ito sa ating mga commuters, dahil alam po natin ang epekto ng krisis sa Middle East (The President said that, whether or not there will be a fare increase, he hopes it will not adversely affect our commuters. We all know the impact of the crisis in the Middle East)," she said. Castro also said that the proposal will be discussed "later today." The recommendation of the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) to provide a P20 Fuel subsidy to public utility vehicles (PUVs) will also be discussed during a meeting with Executive Secretary Ralph Recto. "So, pag-uusapan po ng Office of the Executive Secretary, DOTr, and Economic Team para po mas magkaroon nang kongkreto at detalyeng resolusyon patungkol po diyan (So, the Office of the Executive Secretary, the Department of Transportation (DOTr), and the Economic Team will discuss the matter to come up with a more concrete and detailed resolution), Castro said.
